2611.21373.t: WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for Omni AI-Generated Video Detection
2611.21373.s: WeVisForensics coordinates self-evolving visual and audio forensic inspector agents under a dual-timescale reinforcement learning policy to detect generated-video artifacts with localized evidence and high accuracy.

2611.26444.t: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
2611.26444.s: A diagnostic benchmark of 180 simulated manipulation configurations evaluates whether embodied systems can combine history-based reasoning, precise execution, and closed-loop environmental feedback, revealing that single-view competence does not transfer to composed tasks.

2611.26409.t: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
2611.26409.s: WeMM-Video is a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models that unify text, image, audio, and video processing for joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, using hybrid thinking modes and large-scale training to achieve strong open-source video understanding results.

2611.26590.t: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models

2611.26629.s: Posterior Matching Distillation trains a stochastic student to match a teacher diffusion model’s full posterior via tilted mean constraints, enabling high-quality few-step image generation without auxiliary score networks.

2611.26595.t: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
2611.26595.s: A task-adaptive agentic framework utilizes 3D proxies, physics simulation, and multi-agent coordination to enhance the structural control, physical plausibility, and visual realism of generated videos.

2611.21383.t: The Mask Is Not the Object: Volumetric Supervision for 3D Gaussian Segmentation
2611.21383.s: A plug-and-play objective, VODA, groups per-pixel contributors by local depth to supervise all Gaussians in selected depth clusters, improving volumetric segmentation and enabling evaluation via Removal-3D and Removal Depth Error.

2611.26603.t: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
2611.26603.s: A single scalable network estimates dense metric depth for images and video at native resolution, jointly improving metric accuracy, boundary sharpness, and temporal consistency.

2611.26073.t: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
2611.26073.s: A statistical test, AltRA-Test, determines when large language models can replace human annotators by comparing inter-annotator agreement in resampled mixed human-LLM panels, and evaluations show it often requires about 100 items and makes better replacement decisions than baselines.

2611.26414.t: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
2611.26414.s: ZeroVLN is a slow-fast vision-language navigation framework that avoids navigation-domain supervised fine-tuning of the VLM brain by using a semantic tool-calling interface and closed-loop reinforcement learning to coordinate a language-based brain with an action expert, improving VLN-CE performance while preserving general visual capabilities.

2611.26627.t: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
2611.26627.s: A fixed set of steering vectors added to a frozen diffusion transformer recovers most of the quality gains from reinforcement learning post-training, indicating that much of the improvement comes from a constant shift rather than prompt-specific transformations.

2611.25980.t: Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models
2611.25980.s: AFFECT, an auxiliary objective that trains world models to match visual responses to temporally correlated action noise, improves rollout fidelity and planning success in simulated and real robotic tasks.

2611.24193.t: WM^MLLM: Turning MLLMs into World Models
2611.24193.s: WM^MLLM uses multimodal large language models to maintain an external panorama state with revision history, enabling persistent, editable world generation from a single image with exact revisits and local edits.

2611.24809.t: On-Policy Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models
2611.24809.s: FlashMorph2 performs on-policy layer selection and weight adaptation for hybrid attention Transformers, improving long-context benchmark scores while selecting layers efficiently across model scales.

2611.21053.t: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI
2611.21053.s: A local System 1 agent framework compiles tool schemas and requests into multiple-choice questions answered by a one-pass decision model, enabling accurate biomedical tool calls without text generation or invented content.

2611.22666.t: VSpark: Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.22666.s: VSpark accelerates autoregressive vision-language-action models by improving speculative decoding with calibrated action-noise rollouts, hidden-feature alignment, and reuse of rejected-draft continuations, achieving lossless 1.28x–2.10x speedups across multiple robot manipulation tasks.

2611.26211.t: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
2611.26211.o: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
2611.26211.s: SpecWM is a training-free inference framework for streaming video world models that verifies draft chunks using the target model's latent velocity field and applies reusable corrections via threshold-based accept/refine/reject decisions to improve visual quality, control, and speed.

2611.25179.t: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
2611.25179.o: Mohamed Bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
2611.25179.s: An LLM-based pipeline audits simulated manipulation success checkers by recreating disagreement scenarios and visually verifying whether observed behavior satisfies task instructions, revealing phantom successes and silent failures.

2611.19499.t: Do Probing and Steering Favor the Same Directions Within and Across Language Models?
2611.19499.o: Fraunhofer Institute for Intelligent Analysis and Information Systems
2611.19499.s: The best direction for probing a concept in a language model's hidden state is not the best direction for steering the model toward that concept, with implications for transfer and abstention.

2611.26298.t: DailySafe: Benchmarking Dynamic Safety Awareness in Everyday Multi-Turn Multimodal Interactions
2611.26298.s: A new benchmark, DailySafe, evaluates the ability of multimodal large language models to maintain safety and address evolving risks within complex, multi-turn, real-world interactions.

2611.23875.t: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
2611.23875.s: A coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone by reparametrizing it with interpretable optical elements, achieving better classification and image encoding than gradient-free methods and approaching backpropagation through a calibrated model at lower cost.

2611.25776.t: Suppressing the Shortcut Hidden Behind the Gains of VideoLLM Fine-Tuning
2611.25776.s: VETO suppresses shortcut learning in VideoLLMs by projecting supervised fine-tuning updates onto the orthogonal complement of the text-only activation subspace, improving out-of-distribution video reasoning.

2611.26624.t: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
2611.26624.s: PlayCraft uses a vision-based player agent and a crafter agent to iteratively revise games, improving player learning gains and slopes across intelligence settings.

2611.26540.s: AURA enables low-latency, causal video generation for streaming applications by utilizing a rolling KV cache and a two-stage distillation pipeline to significantly reduce the required diffusion steps.

2611.25005.t: Inhabitant: An Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Human-Scene Interaction with Spatial Control and Quantitative Feedback
2611.25005.s: Inhabitant enables a language-model agent to plan and execute long-horizon human-scene interactions by specifying motions spatially, measuring deviations, and revising control, achieving high task completion on the Inhabit benchmark.

2611.24738.t: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
2611.24738.s: Jeveration repurposes a frozen vision-language model to generate coherent images and perform image-to-image and dense prediction tasks in a single forward pass with fast 512x512 generation.

2611.14848.t: Tideway: Phase-Aware Tiered Memory Management for MoE Inference on Consumer Devices
2611.14848.s: TIDEWAY enables efficient inference of large Mixture-of-Experts models on memory-constrained consumer devices by treating host RAM and GPU VRAM as a unified memory pool with phase-aware layouts and optimized CUDA Graph execution under expert paging.

2611.21366.t: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive

2611.23068.t: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
2611.23068.s: Agent evolution is often bottlenecked by noisy evaluations that cannot reliably identify better candidate artifacts or rank methods, so progress requires making true improvements detectable and accumulable.

2611.24654.t: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
2611.24654.s: CurvDelta and CurvLoRA constrain LLM updates to a low-curvature preservation space, improving retention while maintaining target adaptation across reasoning, code, and unlearning tasks.

2611.17600.t: LightTAR: Light and Fast Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning
2611.17600.s: LightTAR adapts dimensionality reduction to the prediction task by adding target-aware features from encoder layers via regularized partial least squares, improving multimodal tabular model performance with minimal runtime overhead.

2611.24869.t: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
2611.24869.s: A rule-graph-based generative world model preserves user-defined rules and world states across saving and loading while accurately realizing rule-induced visual changes on designated objects and attributes.

2611.24408.t: StrideWorld: Benchmarking Scene Rigidity and Action Consistency in Interactive Video World Model
2611.24408.s: StrideWorld is a benchmark that fixes references before motion to detect scene deformation and action inconsistency in interactive video world models, showing that most models deform scenes and only depth-scaled command models preserve composed routes.

2611.23779.t: TabBioMed: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Biomedical Tabular Learning
2611.23779.s: A large-scale benchmark of 94 curated biomedical tabular datasets standardizes evaluation across classification, regression, and multi-target tasks and finds that foundation models lead overall while tree-based models and tuned multilayer perceptrons remain competitive under cost constraints.

2611.22287.t: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
2611.22287.s: A method that removes the decoder from latent diffusion models by adding a final-step prediction head to a finetuned diffusion transformer, reducing inference cost and improving pixel quality in image and video generation.

2611.24098.t: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
2611.24098.s: A new benchmark and agentic workflows assess vision-language models for automatic video rough-cut, revealing current models struggle to match expert cut plans.

2611.21553.t: BLIP-Live: Balancing Timeliness & Firing Precision in Proactive Streaming Video Agents
2611.21553.s: BLIP-Live unifies data, metrics, inference, and training for proactive streaming video understanding, using the PAUC-F metric and achieving state-of-the-art results on proactive streaming benchmarks.

2611.23808.t: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards
2611.23808.s: A diagnostic benchmark and two-phase reinforcement learning framework enable personalized vision-language assistants to jointly connect visual hazard evidence with personal memory for appropriate responses.

2611.24161.t: AVTR: Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination
2611.24161.s: Adaptive Visual-Textual Reasoning combines generative visual reflection with textual reasoning and learns to route between them per input, improving multimodal task accuracy while reducing inference latency.

2611.24362.t: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents
2611.24362.s: A novel framework addresses the limitations of current reinforcement learning-based red-teaming methods by employing dictionary learning and on-policy adversarial training to improve the robustness of LLM agents against indirect prompt injection attacks.

2611.08136.t: How Far Can Untrained Neural Networks Go in Anomaly Detection? From Tables to Pixels
2611.08136.s: Untrained neural networks with fixed random nonlinear features and Mahalanobis scoring can detect anomalies competitively on tabular and visual tasks without weight optimization or pretrained representations.

2611.24941.t: UltraTex: Aligning Physical Knowledge for High-Fidelity PBR Texture Generation
2611.24941.s: UltraTex employs a cascaded multi-view framework that integrates physical knowledge and vision-language model features to accurately generate physically plausible PBR texture maps.

2611.24681.t: DrawScore: Evaluating Generated CAD Models against Engineering Drawings
2611.24681.s: A new metric for automatic CAD generation evaluates models through engineering-drawing projections with a saturating penalty along curves, exposing small local errors that volume- or surface-based metrics miss and enabling use as a reinforcement learning reward or test-time verifier.

2611.23499.s: BiCAT shares a motion representation across arms and conditions each arm's tokens on its partner via symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder, enabling parallel arm token prediction and improving bimanual manipulation success.

2611.23236.t: PGPO: Prototype-Guided Progressive Obfuscation for Privacy-Preserving LLM-Enhanced Recommendation
2611.23236.s: A prototype-guided progressive obfuscation method preserves relative item relations while perturbing high-influence semantic embeddings to defend against inversion attacks in LLM-enhanced recommender systems.

2611.22673.s: FVSCORE is a neuro-symbolic evaluation framework that compiles videos into prompt and implicit constraint propositions, verifies them with perceptual tools and soft temporal logic, and calibrates significant violations to produce interpretable, human-aligned feedback for video generation.

2607.21179.t: Out of Sight, Still in Mind: Token Compression for Omni-LLMs
2607.21179.s: ReMo, a training-free method, reduces inference input token cost for omni-modal large language models by compressing redundant visual tokens through cross-modal alignment and replacing object-level visual tokens with compact text descriptions, achieving comparable accuracy on audio-visual tasks.

2611.22115.t: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks

2611.17621.t: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs
2611.17621.s: AscendGYM provides a benchmark for assessing kernel optimization capabilities on Ascend NPUs using real-workload test cases, two evaluation modes, and a Speedup-Token Score that balances speedup against token cost.

2611.22055.o: Pohang University of Science and Technology
2611.22055.s: When large language models write neural network weights without gradient-based training, they tend to design sparse table or associative-memory models that outperform same-sized Transformers with far fewer parameters and faster GPU inference, though pretrained LLMs remain more accurate.

2611.19800.s: Branching Transformer blocks into parallel parameterized branches, combined with shared KV caching, improves language model quality and inference efficiency compared with standard sequential Transformers.

2611.21099.t: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models

2611.18856.t: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
2611.18856.s: Continual recursive self-improvement lets harness optimizers reuse and revise prior edits across changing benchmarks or policy models by storing rationales, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation contexts in a self-improvement memory, improving final scores over continuation baselines.

2611.15348.t: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose
2611.15348.s: A comprehensive benchmark evaluates time-series classification methods on a large clinical breath dataset under realistic temporal splits, showing that sensor drift lowers performance and recurrent models are most consistent across diseases.

2611.21392.t: VideoNexus: Video Perception Beyond the Reasoning Context
2611.21392.s: VideoNexus separates detailed video perception from evidence-driven planning and reasoning, using perception sub-agents to return compact temporally grounded evidence and achieving higher accuracy at lower cost on long-video benchmarks.

2611.23144.t: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
2611.23144.s: This unified foundation model enables the recovery of dense geometry, camera poses, and object tracking from diverse, uncalibrated observations in 4D scenes using a shared geometry and motion branch architecture.

2611.21152.t: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
2611.21152.s: RepoFactory converts real repositories into verifiable coding environments and optimizes them via an Environment Evolution Loop using proxy feedback, enabling trained coding agents to achieve strong gains on long-horizon coding and agentic benchmarks.

2611.17048.t: Beyond Answering: Learning to Speak First and Act in Streaming Video
2611.17048.s: AURA 2.0 is a streaming video large language model that can initiate conversations, call tools, and perform interactive visual grounding, with long-horizon memory and a three-stage training scheme for improved streaming interaction.

2611.22563.t: CADMAGEDDON: High-Fidelity CAD Reconstruction with Local Inference
2611.22563.s: CADMAGEDDON is an open-source agent that reconstructs editable CAD from meshes locally on single-GPU systems and laptops, using a mid-sized Qwen model and geometric tools to outperform prior systems.

2611.21925.t: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
2611.21925.s: A lightweight feature-encoding method with rejection memory and architectural enhancements enables faster large language model inference by improving speculative-diffusion draft verification.

2611.08922.t: Glyph: An Interpretability Engine for AI-Driven Scientific Discovery in Clinical Data
2611.08922.s: Glyph uses foundation models and sparse autoencoders to extract interpretable clinical concepts from multimodal records and CT data, revealing reproducible predictive associations across patient cohorts.

2611.19244.t: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
2611.19244.s: On-policy distillation can improve or degrade language-model agent interaction across domains, and selectively retaining teacher-preferred positions mitigates negative transfer at a cost to source-domain learning.

2611.12069.s: MPEG-Diffusion reduces the computational cost of video diffusion transformers by generating only a self-selected high-resolution region with dual-resolution attention and a mixed-resolution decoder, achieving faster denoising without quality loss.

2611.23219.t: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
2611.23219.s: Capable frozen LLM agents can autonomously construct context-based self-learning algorithms from basic resources and a general goal, yielding text artifacts that transfer to new game and 3D navigation tasks.

2611.21644.t: MInfoVisQA: A Multilingual Benchmark for Information-Rich Visual Question Answering
2611.21644.o: Mohamed Bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
2611.21644.s: MInfoVisQA, a 24-language parallel benchmark, reveals substantial cross-language robustness gaps in multimodal large language models for information-rich visual question answering.

2611.19559.t: ResWAM: Learning What Changes, Not What Stays, for World-Action Models
2611.19559.s: ResWAM combines visual residual learning in frozen DINOv3 features with a lightweight dual-branch DiT trained via conditional flow matching to improve vision-language-action policy success while lowering training and inference compute.

2611.18553.t: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
2611.18553.s: The WEIGHTBENCH benchmark evaluates the capacity of large language models to perform Weight-Space Programming tasks, which involve reading, modifying, and generating the weights of various neural network architectures.

2611.23140.t: GameRealm: Grounding Visual Learning in Interactive Games
2611.23140.s: GameRealm is a large-scale multimodal gameplay dataset with synchronized depth, camera, audio, control, and 3D trajectory annotations that improves visual foundation models for generation and geometric learning.

2611.19857.s: PanDWM stitches six camera views into a 360° panoramic band and uses a distilled causal student with a feed-forward 3D Gaussian decoder to generate consistent 4D driving scenes faster and with better FID/FVD than multi-camera baselines.

2611.21218.t: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
2611.21218.s: InclusionMed is an open medical AI evaluation initiative that audits and reproduces benchmarks across healthcare roles and capabilities, revealing that model rankings and inference costs vary by context and motivating broader, context-specific evaluation.

2611.21003.t: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models

2611.19937.t: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data
2611.19937.s: An end-to-end flow-matching framework generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories via a cross-asset flow Transformer and a two-stage imitation and group-relative reinforcement learning procedure, improving risk-adjusted returns on cryptocurrency perpetual futures.

2611.20218.t: SWE-CoWork: Benchmarking Coding Agents as Digital Employees in Organizations
2611.20218.s: A benchmark of realistic software engineering assignments reveals that current coding agents struggle to track requirements from clarification through implementation, verification, and handoff, completing few tasks despite partial test success.

2611.07222.t: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection

2611.21607.t: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters

2611.17834.t: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
2611.17834.s: An AI reviewer trained by reinforcement learning to jointly maximize precision and recall of soundness review points outperforms frontier models and other training methods and transfers to other review domains.

2611.20254.s: VoxMel is a tokenizer-free autoregressive TTS framework that uses an invertible two-axis Haar transform to decompose mel spectrograms into Coarse-Mel and residual tiers, enabling stable high-fidelity generation with strong recognition and speaker-similarity results.

2611.17110.t: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
2611.17110.s: SALA aligns latent actions across human and robot videos by using language-based semantic similarities to form a shared latent action space that supervises embodied foundation model training and improves robot task performance.

2611.20986.t: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model
2611.20986.s: A large language model can output single-chain protein structures from its internal residue states by invoking a pretrained structure head, with reduced long-chain accuracy and MMLU-Pro accuracy in the reported tests.

2611.08977.t: Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model
2611.08977.s: Energy-Based Reasoners guide looped latent reasoning by learning an energy function whose gradient refines states and signals when to stop, with exploration-based training improving performance and efficiency.

2611.14960.t: Termination Lag: Coding Agents Solve Early but Stop Late
2611.14960.s: Coding agents often find correct patches early but continue working, sometimes undoing correct solutions, with termination lag varying by model and benchmark.

2611.20441.t: Abstention Direction in Large Language Models: Mechanistic Interpretability of Abstention Across Query Ambiguity, Knowledge Limits, and Safety Alignment
2611.20441.s: Abstention in large language models arises from query ambiguity, model knowledge limits, and value misalignment, and steering internal activations in middle layers can increase or decrease abstention across these causes.

2611.18919.t: Correcting Persistent Failures in Point-Cloud Grasping Policies using Human Demonstrations in Virtual Reality
2611.18919.s: A human-in-the-loop failure-mining pipeline turns persistently unsolved grasps of a reinforcement-learning point-cloud policy into virtual-reality human demonstrations, improving hard-case success without reducing generalization to unseen objects.

2611.17933.t: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination
2611.17933.s: OutfitterBench evaluates LLM agents managing a 200-day outdoor-equipment rental business under fixed capital and uncertain demand, revealing limitations in sustaining feasible commitments and reallocating resources.

2611.20404.t: Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier
2611.20404.s: Latent feedback, which feeds each token's top-layer state into the next token's input, improves compute and data efficiency over standard Transformers, especially when unique data is abundant relative to model size.

2611.20385.t: DominoBench: Evaluating Multi-Step Physical Reasoning from Still Images
2611.20385.s: A new benchmark, DominoBench, shows that current vision-language and multimodal models cannot reliably predict physical outcomes from still images unless the critical calculation and necessary quantities are provided.

2611.09825.t: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
2611.09825.s: BitDecoding-FP4 co-designs FP4 quantization and system optimizations to enable accurate, high-throughput long-context KV decoding for LLMs.

2611.19537.t: Continuation-Guided LLM Evolution of Program Policies and Goal Compilers in Craftax
2611.19537.s: A framework uses coding agents and a feedback cascade to synthesize code-based policies that achieve long-horizon success and can be factored into a reusable goal compiler for zero-shot transfer to new tasks.

2611.18668.t: UMM-JEPA: Generative Pretraining via Masked Next-Scale Representation Prediction for Unified Multimodal Models
2611.18668.s: Reformulating generation as progressive prediction of continuous perceptual representations improves visual understanding in unified multimodal models more than discrete-code or latent-flow objectives.

2611.19649.t: LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
2611.19649.s: LoopFill reduces decoding latency for looped language models by combining multi-token suffix drafts and shallow-loop predictions into a single draft tree with full-depth verification that preserves the autoregressive output distribution.

2611.13685.t: Ego Guidance: Enhancing Robot Policy Learning with Action-Free Human Egocentric Videos
2611.13685.s: A mixture-of-transformers architecture jointly predicts future visual states and actions, leveraging pretrained vision-language representations and egocentric videos to improve robot policy learning without action supervision.

2611.16642.s: A dataset distillation method learns synthetic samples that approximate per-class data distributions in a feature extractor's latent space, improving distribution coverage and classification training while supporting visualization and other modalities.

2611.21439.t: A Reinforcement Learning Method to Navigate SMEFT Operator Space
2611.21439.s: A reinforcement learning agent with a lightweight actor-critic architecture explores the Standard Model Effective Field Theory operator space to discover diverse high-quality theory hypotheses and improve global fits.

2611.20192.t: GlyphAtlas: Disentangling Stroke Detail from Layout for Scene Text Synthesis
2611.20192.s: GlyphAtlas uses a dedicated glyph atlas and atlas-anchored attention to provide fine-grained stroke references for scene text synthesis, improving stroke accuracy and zero-shot transfer.

2611.18397.t: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
2611.18397.s: Gamer is a generalist agent framework that integrates perception, memory, and multi-step reasoning, trained through continued pre-training, sparse-thinking instruction tuning, and multi-turn reinforcement learning to interact efficiently in 2D and 3D environments.

2611.18359.t: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
2611.18359.s: Agentic robotics, centered on an Embodied System 2 formed by a foundation model and embodied harness, requires a shared evaluation framework and research roadmap to achieve reliable physical autonomy.

2611.15789.t: VibePrevisBench: Evaluating Agentic Coding for 4D Scene Generation in Blender

2611.12068.s: MIRIX-2.0 is a multi-agent memory system for LLM agents that achieves high accuracy and efficiency across QA and procedural benchmarks without fine-tuning.

2611.18482.t: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
2611.18482.s: MMFlash improves multimodal speculative decoding by adaptively upweighting visually dependent tokens and using sparse attention for long video, yielding up to 3.58× lossless speedup.

2611.17831.t: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations
2611.17831.s: Counterfactual supervision over pixel transformations enables language models to read motion dynamics from frozen predictive video encoders, yielding V-JEPA-LM models that outperform open video LLMs across benchmarks.

2611.07226.t: Loopback Transformer: Towards a Unified View of Residual Looped Transformers
2611.07226.s: A looped Transformer that separately controls input strength, total update weight, and per-update allocation achieves lower validation loss and higher downstream accuracy than standard and looped residual baselines while using fewer parameters.

2611.18338.s: A history-aware benchmark and memory-powered method improve Text-to-SQL accuracy and reduce cost by reusing verified SQL components and consulting schemas on demand.

2611.13509.t: Mobile AI Factory: Building Specialized Language Models for Your Mobile Device
2611.13509.s: Mobile AI Factory is an agentic system that automatically builds task- and phone-specific fine-tuned quantized small language models, using an orchestrator LLM, real device measurements, and adaptive search to match or outperform larger models with much less GPU time.

2611.17194.t: eDMD: Endpoint Distribution Matching for Few-Step Diffusion Distillation
2611.17194.s: Endpoint Distribution Matching Distillation trains a shared fake model only on final student outputs and adds precise teacher supervision to better align few-step diffusion students with teacher distributions for 4-step generation.

2611.12901.t: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding
2611.12901.s: StepRefine, a plug-and-play decoding strategy, mitigates hallucinations in multimodal diffusion language models by switching between discrete denoising and latent refinement based on entropy spikes and distributional stability.

2611.14487.t: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
2611.14487.s: A Twenty Questions-style benchmark for research ideation shows that large language models make most progress early, can recognize good ideas or questions but often cannot generate them, and may benefit from externally sourced candidates in automated research systems.

2611.16378.t: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents
2611.16378.s: A governance framework separates generation from adoption of self-modifying autonomous-agent changes, using fresh paired audits, non-inferiority checks, and calibrated statistical bounds to confirm improvements before bounded deployment.

2611.17820.s: Alignment training on individual LLM agents often fails to transfer to multi-agent teams, but designating a safety lead and having a coordinator publish safety specifications can restore single-agent alignment.

2611.18550.t: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations
2611.18550.s: Distilled few-step diffusion models exhibit diversity collapse because activation variance is concentrated into fewer directions in an intermediate block at the initial denoising step, and ReDiverse restores sample diversity by reintroducing teacher variance directions through adapter fine-tuning or training-free activation steering while preserving generation quality.

2611.02822.t: Disen-Forcing: Disentangling Semantic Anchoring from Motion for Autoregressive Video Diffusion
2611.02822.s: Disen-Forcing is a distillation-time method for autoregressive video diffusion models that disentangles attention-head specialization to improve long-range consistency and motion dynamics in long-horizon video generation.

2611.15640.t: MemInStream: Memorizing or Merely Recognizing? Rethinking Streaming Video Memory Evaluation
2611.15640.s: MemInStream is a benchmark that evaluates memory capabilities in streaming video understanding using evidence-controlled validation to separate memory limitations from visual understanding failures.

2611.16010.t: Iris-Z: Scaling One Generative Model Past Specialist Geometry Models
2611.16010.s: A unified generative backbone jointly models image appearance and depth, surpassing specialized depth models at scale while preserving general image generation.

2611.14505.t: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
2611.14505.s: Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-AGI tasks, compares memory- and weight-based continual learning under frozen-weight agent harnesses, revealing that harness persistence rarely improves memorization and most harness methods underperform simple caching, while weight-based learning shows better generalization.

2611.17321.s: A set-conditioned SE(3) flow model pretrained on procedurally generated LEGO assemblies and finetuned with image conditioning, combined with analytic connectivity-field guidance, infers part poses to assemble objects from images.

2611.15777.t: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
2611.15777.s: SO-Arena evaluates System One models across domains and capability families, revealing that scaling and reasoning gains vary and that high overall accuracy does not ensure reliable decision-making.

2611.15131.t: Duo: A Reciprocal World Model for Full-Duplex Interaction
2611.15131.s: A reciprocal world model enables real-time full-duplex audiovisual interaction by jointly modeling intent and realization using autoregressive reasoning, synchronized attention, and dual rollout distillation.

2611.16748.t: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
2611.16748.s: PhysLoop leverages large language models to guide video generation, selection, and correction, enabling physically consistent self-improvement and controllable data construction for video models.

2611.17167.t: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
2611.17167.s: A decision model that acts poorly can still teach reinforcement learning policies effectively by judging complete action trajectories, improving success on ALFWorld and WebShop.

2611.17331.t: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
2611.17331.s: By baking global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, Test-Time Baking (TTB) enhances the fidelity of novel-view decoding in Large View Synthesis Models while maintaining the efficiency of Test-Time Training.

2611.17334.s: Controlled experiments show that multimodal language models do not need a pretrained vision encoder, but benefit from dedicated vision capacity trained jointly with the backbone and integrated early rather than before fusion.

2611.08318.t: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
2611.08318.s: Exposing benchmark success criteria to self-improving embodied coding agents can raise measured success under those criteria without improving instructed-task completion, and the advantage weakens under slight criteria changes and transfers poorly across tasks, while instruction-faithful criteria better reflect instructed-task performance.

2611.16905.t: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
2611.16905.s: FOAM is a lightweight SOAP variant that uses input-only preconditioning and a factored Adam-moment estimator to match strong second-order and Muon baselines in LLM pre-training while using half the optimizer state and running at Muon-class speed.

2611.16409.t: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement
2611.16409.s: Language-model agents trained with reinforcement learning can improve by learning to create and curate experience artifacts that help future rollouts, not just by optimizing actions from scalar rewards.

2611.08219.t: Agent-R^2: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis
2611.08219.s: A real-source data synthesis framework trains a 4B agent on 4k task instances with supervised fine-tuning and rubric-based reinforcement learning, improving realistic productivity work and file-grounded reasoning over larger models.

2611.16009.t: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
2611.16009.s: A simplified evaluation harness that keeps full episode history and stops motions early substantially improves robot-use agent scores on RoboDojo, with scene geometry providing the largest additional benefit.

2611.14256.t: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
2611.14256.s: A survey analyzes why self-improvement mechanisms for multimodal agents transfer unevenly across reasoning, generation, navigation, and manipulation scenarios, framing them as trade-offs over scarce factors and task-structural resources.

2611.14046.t: Structured Confidence Perturbation via Fisher Geometry for Adversarial Training
2611.14046.s: A hybrid adversarial training approach combining cross-entropy and KL divergence with geometry-aware perturbations on the confidence manifold improves robustness and transferability by targeting confidence structure deformation.

2610.40394.t: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks
2610.40394.s: A large-scale corpus of structured proof-supervision records derived from university mathematics textbooks improves language model mathematical reasoning by 16.7 percentage points over a base model when used for fine-tuning.

2611.13410.t: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
2611.13410.s: Low-bit quantized LLM agents can recover much of their task success through closed-loop guidance from a full-precision teacher, followed by unassisted student training on corrected and reference turns.

2611.08286.t: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds
2611.08286.s: Interactive Visual Gym enables closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models by jointly simulating task environments and human users, exposing limitations in state-of-the-art VLMs and improving performance through closed-loop training.

2603.27343.t: WMIP: A Working-Memory-Inspired Programmable Probe of Cumulative State Tracking in Large Language Models
2603.27343.s: Large language models struggle with cumulative state tracking across multiple updates despite strong single-step arithmetic, and their measured accuracy depends heavily on output protocols.

2611.12869.t: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
2611.12869.s: Cross-modal representational alignment between unimodal language and vision models increases with model capability when captions are clean and informative, but remains below same-modality alignment and can exceed explicitly aligned vision-language models.

2611.14418.t: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits at Uncertain Decoding Steps in a Small Local Model
2611.14418.s: A dynamic weight precision allocation strategy is proposed, utilizing low-bit quantization and uncertainty-based gating to selectively upgrade weight precision during LLM generation, thereby optimizing computational cost.

2611.08379.t: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks
2611.08379.s: GraphMuon adapts Muon's matrix orthogonalization to the covariance of graph-propagated representations, reducing graph-induced update amplification and speeding validation-loss time-to-target on graph benchmarks.

2611.14320.t: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
2611.14320.s: WikiTrace links each distilled lesson to its source trajectory and rationale, enabling LLM agents to verify and correct memories before acting, improving performance and reducing memory-induced degradation across agentic benchmarks.

2611.14033.t: Few-Step Streaming Video Generation via Condition Shifting
2611.14033.s: APEX extends a streaming video generation method by replacing a separate fake-score network with condition shifting to estimate the generated distribution’s velocity field, improving instruction following and visual aesthetics while reducing memory and iteration time relative to DMD.

2611.14210.t: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
2611.14210.s: Tree-Ising repairs reasoning loops in LLM weights by solving sparse Ising/QUBO problems over BF16 parameters, improving math benchmark accuracy with fewer weight edits and no gradient or LLM-token cost.

2611.12426.t: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations
2611.12426.s: A discrete native-resolution vision transformer with grouped product quantization and a dual-branch objective acts as a versatile visual tokenizer, matching or exceeding task-specific baselines across visual understanding, generation, and editing tasks.

2611.10649.t: MACaQ: Fast, Model Agnostic Calibrated Quantization for Low-Precision Weights and Activations
2611.10649.s: MACaQ is an MXFP4 W4A4 post-training quantization method that quantizes each linear layer independently using online activation transforms and Hessian-aware refinement, reducing cost while preserving accuracy across language and diffusion models.

2611.13348.t: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
2611.13348.s: ProTEUS is a mutation-resolved world model that combines sequence, evolutionary, and structural representations with fast all-atom prediction and closed-loop feedback to guide protein evolution and improve mutant activity.

2611.03142.t: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
2611.03142.s: DepthGraft improves deep language model training by hierarchically sharing key-value representations across layers, reducing memory use while boosting accuracy.

2611.10015.t: Micius-Flash: Lightweight Agentic Intelligence for Engineering
2611.10015.s: Micius-Flash is a 27B-parameter multimodal reasoning model trained with a knowledge-tree data pipeline and multi-teacher on-policy distillation, achieving strong hardware and semiconductor agent benchmark results and supporting tool-integrated engineering workflows.

2611.14488.t: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
2611.14488.s: Memory in vision-language-action policies can mistake pauses for progress because it is indexed by time, causing early stopping, while event-based indexing mitigates this without retraining.

2611.12411.t: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation
2611.12411.s: PhysOPSD uses executable code as privileged physical context to improve the physical plausibility of video generative models through on-policy self-distillation with dual-level privilege and controlled variations.

2611.13560.t: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
2611.13560.s: At matched compute, dense process rewards such as Monte-Carlo rewards underperform standard GRPO for language-model reasoning, while selecting prompts with predicted success near 1/2 yields small consistent accuracy gains.

2611.13572.t: Market-Conditioned JEPA: Learning from Unpredictable Market Shocks
2611.13572.s: A market-conditioned joint-embedding predictive architecture improves financial time-series prediction by conditioning on a leave-one-out market factor, enhancing market exposure, risk, liquidity, and return forecasts.

2611.12200.t: Learning to Act with World Models by Valuing What Comes Next
2611.12200.s: WM-PPO combines a world model with PPO’s critic to create auxiliary policy advantages and value targets from predicted successor states, improving task success without privileged information.

2611.13995.t: Lipschitz-Controlled Flow Matching for Robust Image Restoration
2611.13995.s: LipsFlower stabilizes flow-matching image restoration by combining Lipschitz-aware architecture and regularization to reduce perturbation amplification while maintaining competitive restoration quality.

2611.11912.t: LO-World: Unified BEV Latent Modeling for Joint 4D Occupancy and LiDAR Forecasting
2611.11912.s: A unified 4D world model jointly forecasts LiDAR point clouds and 3D semantic occupancy in a shared BEV latent space, improving accuracy and real-time throughput.

2611.12806.t: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
2611.12806.s: LingBot-Touch is a tactile foundation model that learns a unified, extensible representation across heterogeneous tactile sensors, yielding plug-and-play tactile tokens that consistently enhance manipulation policies such as diffusion policy and VLA models.

2611.10771.t: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence
2611.10771.s: WorldFoundry offers open-source infrastructure for reproducible inference and evaluation of generative world models across video, 3D/4D, embodied action, and interactive systems, with traceable evidence and benchmarks.

2611.12886.t: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
2611.12886.s: Reframe is a two-stage post-training framework that aligns visual agents’ observation states through evidence-aware reinforcement learning and observation-gated on-policy distillation, improving tool use and outperforming Mix-RL and vanilla MOPD across image and video benchmarks.

2610.42148.t: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
2610.42148.s: Flide is an exact inference engine that accelerates decision-model LLM agents by decoupling logical request trees from physical execution and using ForkAttention to preserve exact branch evaluations.

2611.08240.t: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
2611.08240.s: Reinforcement learning objectives for diffusion models are reformulated for few-step samplers through x-space transformation, gradient decomposition, and anchor adaptation, yielding modular few-step variants of several methods and showing reward-gradient methods excel with differentiable rewards while DiffusionNFT-style methods achieve high rewards in fewer iterations.

2611.11450.t: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?
2611.11450.s: On-policy distillation tolerates substantial training-inference mismatch from quantized inference and asynchronous rollouts, with model- and layer-specific limits, and a lightweight admission check plus FP8 recipes can exploit this tolerance to improve training efficiency.

2611.01112.t: Auriga Technical Report: A Task-Agnostic Agent Harness for Zero-Shot Embodied Manipulation
2611.01112.s: Auriga, a task-agnostic agent harness, closes most of the planning-execution gap in zero-shot robot manipulation by combining explicit task beliefs, calibrated 3D measurements, dual-arm control, and execution monitoring, achieving state-of-the-art results on RoboDojo and RoboCasa365.

2611.02810.t: TRIO: Task Refinement with Individual Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
2611.02810.s: TRIO coordinates three specialized agents through iterative refinement and individual optimization objectives to improve retrieval-augmented generation by enhancing query expansion, retrieval judgment, and answer accuracy.

2611.11890.t: Training Vision Transformers to Focus: Emergence of Spatial Attention Head Specialization
2611.11890.s: Two visual focusing losses align a Vision Transformer's multi-head attention with image regions, producing specialized spatial attention heads and improving dense prediction such as zero-shot segmentation without labels.

2611.08935.t: SkinMind: Equipping Agentic RAG with Human-Inspired Graph Probing for Reliable Dermatology AI
2611.08935.s: SkinMind is a multimodal agentic retrieval framework that iteratively probes a large dermatology knowledge graph to gather textual and visual evidence, yielding more accurate answers to dermatology visual questions than direct answering and other retrieval methods.

2611.11344.t: Spatial Harness: Grounding Spatial Reasoning in Executable World States with Physics Engines
2611.11344.s: Spatial Harness improves vision-language models' spatial reasoning by using a Perceiver to construct explicit executable scene states in a physics engine, where a Reasoner simulates viewpoint changes and provides measurements and rendered views to guide answers.

2611.09987.t: Stochastic Deep Supervision for Gallery-Consistent Early-Exit Face Recognition
2611.09987.s: SD-ViT trains Vision Transformers so every block depth yields discriminative face embeddings, enabling early-exit recognition with minimal accuracy loss and no gallery recomputation.

2501.08686.t: Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching
2501.08686.s: A knowledge graph-based retrieval-augmented generation method improves schema matching by retrieving relevant subgraphs and reducing large language model hallucinations without retraining.

2512.23818.t: Energy-Tweedie: Score meets Score, Energy meets Energy
2512.23818.s: A generalized identity links denoising posteriors under Gibbs noise to Stein scores via kernel scoring rules, enabling score estimation, noise-parameter estimation, and diffusion-style sampling.

2611.03953.t: P^2-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors
2611.03953.s: P^2-MOPD jointly optimizes mixing coefficients and student weights under an on-policy distillation objective, enabling faster and more balanced recovery than MOPD by treating experts as parameter priors while keeping the student trainable.

2611.06043.t: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription
2611.06043.s: A full-context speech recognizer is adapted to emit immutable streaming transcripts with near full-context accuracy and low latency by learning longest stable prefix labels.

2611.08264.t: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
2611.08264.s: SplatAnything applies Gaussian Spacing Normalization to canonicalize scene-level Gaussian spacing, yielding more consistent supervision and improved feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting under varying scene scales and viewpoints.

2611.09124.t: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
2611.09124.s: An embodied multi-agent framework uses learned correction codes and a vision-language-action model with motion-aware history and latent world modeling to improve robot control, failure recovery, and training efficiency.

2611.04720.t: OneTrans-GSR: A Generative Slate Ranking Paradigm Unifying Reranking and Mix-Ranking with One Autoregressive Transformer
2611.04720.s: A unified decoder-only policy guided by reward-model-based reinforcement learning generates recommendation exposure slates end-to-end, improving business metrics and reducing reranking and mix-ranking latency in a large-scale system.

2611.06808.t: LLMs Don't Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting
2611.06808.s: A benchmark of dated U.S. financial facts shows that large language models often understate their knowledge and that common safeguards cannot reliably certify that historical backtests are free of information leakage.

2611.09017.t: Frontier3DBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for 3D Creation across Objects, Scenes, and Interactive Open Worlds
2611.09017.s: A unified 145-task benchmark evaluates coding agents across object, scene, and interactive 3D creation, revealing reference fidelity and coordinated activity completion as central bottlenecks.

2611.06748.t: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models
2611.06748.s: EvoWorld combines a vision-language model that maintains and reasons over world state with a segment-autoregressive video renderer to improve event-conditioned causal evolution and revisit consistency in generative video world simulators.

2611.07624.t: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
2611.07624.o: University of Science and Technology of China
2611.07624.s: Agent harness evolution can improve benchmark performance without weight updates, but gains are unreliable, costly, and transfer inconsistently, motivating preservation-aware evaluation and EvoAudit revisions.

2611.01182.t: Fast and Exact Relative-Position Attention via Structure-Aware Kernels
2611.01182.o: Institute for Computer Science, Artificial intelligence and Technology
2611.01182.s: An exact tiled attention algorithm integrates additive relative-position terms into FlashAttention-style computation, reducing memory and compute overhead and accelerating long-context relative-position transformers.

2611.09894.t: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
2611.09894.s: Video-Coder is a code-driven video generation agent that writes and executes code to build structured 3D draft videos, then uses supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with execution and video rewards to improve controllable video generation.

2611.09382.t: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
2611.09382.s: Weight-Space Programming can produce large localized accuracy gains and uneven cross-task transfer, but reliable editing remains inconsistent.

2611.07025.t: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Composable KV Cache Compression at Test-Time
2611.07025.s: A method compresses KV caches by predicting values from keys within each attention head and applying cross-layer low-rank key compression, enabling higher decoding throughput and composability with quantization and eviction.

2610.41711.t: Hierarchical Residuals: A Minimalist Decoupling of Residual Width from Compute Width
2610.41711.s: Hierarchical Residuals decouple residual width from per-layer compute width by connecting standard Transformer blocks through a wider outer residual path, improving efficiency and accuracy without specialized kernels.

2611.08179.t: Knowing When to Teach: Learning from Teachable Prefixes in Multilingual Reasoning Distillation
2611.08179.s: TOPSD improves multilingual reasoning by using likelihood-based drift detection and verification to decide when teacher supervision should be applied during on-policy self-distillation.

2611.10404.t: Coding or Cheating? An Investigation of Frontier Coding LLMs
2611.10404.s: Frontier agentic LLMs trained with verifiable rewards in reinforcement learning environments can learn to reward hack by recovering answers rather than solving tasks, and this behavior persists on unseen hard problems even in hardened settings.

2610.36896.t: PREEN: Exemplar-Based Color Style Transfer with Smartphone Editor Presets
2610.36896.s: PREEN predicts interpretable editor presets for color style transfer by learning from pseudo-presets generated by a style-transfer teacher and refining a CLIP-conditioned regressor with LoRA, enabling fast and adjustable results.

2611.09055.t: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
2611.09055.s: OmniLatent jointly models geometry, deformation, appearance, and part identities in a shared latent space to generate and interactively edit part-aware 3D assets from images or point prompts.

2611.04434.t: Sketchpad: certified exact arithmetic with a small vision-language model
2611.04434.s: A language model with a low-rank adapter and bounded external memory can be certified exact for arbitrary-length arithmetic by checking finitely many views, and it performs multiple exact arithmetic procedures on a laptop browser.

2611.01729.t: ODE Policy: Robot Learning via Action Dynamics, Not Actions
2611.01729.s: ODE policy learns action dynamics with neural ODEs to generate continuous, multimodal robot trajectories, improving imitation and reinforcement learning across diverse tasks.

2611.08449.t: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
2611.08449.s: VFlash employs Flash Primitive Decoding to predict visual primitive coordinates jointly via a lightweight drafter, reducing trajectory prediction error and generation time while improving downstream world action model success.

2611.04277.t: Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses for Generalizable Agent Training
2611.04277.s: A selective harness-rescue training method uses specialized sibling harnesses to replace failed reinforcement learning rollouts and transfer their benefits into a single policy that performs better under the original base harness.

2611.08373.t: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
2611.08373.s: The SLA model enhances spatial understanding in Vision-Language-Action systems by aligning visual embeddings with 3D spatial representations through continual pre-training and feature-dependent gating.

2611.06741.t: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing
2611.06741.s: TailSteer is a final-stage training framework that reduces cumulative visual drift in multi-turn image editing by applying on-policy denoising corrections near the trajectory tail while preserving pretrained generative and editing abilities.

2611.03743.t: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents
2611.03743.s: A state-centric memory framework for large language model agents represents persistent facts with relational and reasoning states to improve long-term personalized dialogue and memory-grounded responses.

2611.05376.t: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
2611.05376.s: Physical AI should include AI-augmented human intelligence via lifelong cognitive symbionts that close cognitive gaps through sensing, context retention, and proactive assistance, requiring embedded governance.

2611.07854.s: Drex is a family of open decision models that directly output probability distributions over answer options instead of autoregressive decoding, using supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning from adjusted feedback, and vision tuning to achieve high accuracy and low latency.

2611.00883.t: Random Is Almost Enough? Stable and Low-Cost Benchmark Compression via BestRand
2611.00883.s: BestRand stabilizes random subset sampling for benchmark compression, reducing high-error risk and estimation error across text, multimodal, agent, and VLA evaluations at lower construction cost.

2611.04894.t: VisSearch-Bench: Evaluating Long Horizon Visual Search in Multimodal Agents
2611.04894.s: A benchmark of 204 visually intensive search tasks shows that even the best multimodal agents with search tools solve only 26.47% of tasks, underscoring the difficulty of linking visual evidence across search steps.

2611.07909.t: EDGAR: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement via Synthetic Failure
2611.07909.s: EDGAR is a conditional diffusion framework with a fusion block and Mixture-of-Experts that refines degraded Gaussian head avatars by injecting self-supervised identity features, using refined multi-view renderings as pseudo-targets to optimize a single avatar.

2611.08376.t: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
2611.08376.s: A linear attention architecture called Muir allocates gate capacity by sensitivity, uses matched-filter readout and a stable parallel update, improving language modeling, long-context recall, and training speed over Gated DeltaNet-2 and Transformer baselines.

2611.04527.t: Future Representation Distillation for Imagination-free World Action Models
2611.04527.s: A robot control method repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a predictive visual encoder via representation distillation, enabling action prediction without generating future videos and achieving real-time control.

2611.08237.t: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling
2611.08237.s: TB-MathModel is a terminal benchmark that makes complete contest-style mathematical modeling problems agentic and verifiable, scoring final numeric answers against multiple human references with feasibility checks.

2611.02660.t: HeLM: Hierarchical Explicit Language Memory for Non-Markovian Manipulation
2611.02660.s: A hierarchical vision-language-action framework stores task-relevant history in explicit language through event detection and memory updates, improving non-Markovian manipulation success while reducing memory use and runtime.

2611.06500.t: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
2611.06500.s: A continuous latent context compression model for LLM agents compresses tool observations into latent tokens and uses action-preserving training to reduce token consumption and runtime while improving task performance.

2611.08089.t: SAE Interprets MoE: Sparse AutoEncoders Reveal That MoE Experts Exhibit Human-Interpretable Fine-Grained Specialization
2611.08089.s: Sparse autoencoders trained on Mixture-of-Experts layer outputs reveal concentrated, interpretable expert contributions that subdivide coarse domains into finer responsibilities.

2610.37739.t: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
2610.37739.s: OpenFrontiers links a large corpus of open research problems with a formally graded benchmark of resolved mathematics problems to evaluate LLM agents, finding limited closed-book rediscovery and live-web success driven mainly by retrieval of published solutions.

2611.07298.t: Reducing Representational Interference in Retrieval Embeddings with Trainable Prefix Tokens
2611.07298.s: A lightweight method that prepends trainable [DUMP] tokens during embedding model training improves retrieval representations by reducing residual token-level signals without changing the architecture, pooling strategy, or loss.

2611.02075.t: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
2611.02075.s: DPDM improves agent decision accuracy by combining frozen language-model representations with a shared pretrained conditional predictor that learns from deployment evidence without parameter updates.

2611.06498.t: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
2611.06498.s: Signed retrieval packs can pass authenticity checks while their embedding vectors are manipulated, so verifiers must validate text-vector consistency and quantisation codes to prevent retrieval hijacking on edge devices.

2611.04386.t: StepX-OPD: Rethinking Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Diffusion Models
2611.04386.s: StepX-OPD jointly trains a text-to-image diffusion model to acquire capabilities and few-step sampling simultaneously, outperforming sequential approaches while reducing training cost.

2610.41789.t: Hard Sample-Conditioned Decorrelated Attention for Robust Face Recognition
2610.41789.s: ViT-HarDis conditions attention head disentanglement on sample difficulty in face recognition, applying stronger decorrelation to hard samples to improve identity discrimination without architectural changes or extra inference cost.

2611.08369.t: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
2611.08369.s: NPCBench is a clinical apprenticeship benchmark for nasopharyngeal carcinoma that evaluates whether models can integrate subspecialty knowledge and multimodal evidence, track patient state across care pathways, and produce jointly correct diagnostic and care decisions.

2610.40119.t: SynthFaces: Balanced Large Scale Human Dataset
2610.40119.s: A pipeline combining Arc2Face diffusion with flow matching on identity embeddings generates a balanced synthetic face dataset to improve fairness and reduce privacy risks in generative model training.

2611.06728.t: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit
2611.06728.s: TurnWise, a turn-level GRPO framework, improves streaming video understanding by aligning learning with individual streaming decisions through turn-level credit assignment and turn-mean policy optimization, reducing redundancy without a learned critic or extra rollouts.

2611.06910.t: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
2611.06910.s: FrontierPhysics is an end-to-end benchmark of 56 expert-designed physics tasks that evaluates AI agents on literature review, research planning, experimentation, and manuscript production using deterministic verifiers and expert rubrics.

2611.06918.t: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
2611.06918.s: NEO-VLA is an encoder-free vision-language-action framework that jointly evolves patch-tokenized images and language, letting a flow-matching action expert use instruction-conditioned visual representations across depths for stronger and more robust manipulation control.

2611.06483.t: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
2611.06483.o: Chinese Academic of Science Institute of Automation
2611.06483.s: Multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning performance depends on sufficient interaction budgets, and BudgetMix RL, which varies budgets during training, provides robust performance across diverse execution settings.

2610.40131.t: VideoMemBench: How Well Do MLLMs Remember in Video Conversations?
2610.40131.s: VideoMemBench evaluates multimodal language models on long multi-turn video dialogues requiring retrieval of earlier visual and conversational context, revealing substantial performance gaps.

2611.05320.t: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
2611.05320.s: A coding agent automates robot demonstration generation by simulating tasks, rendering photorealistic videos, and producing deployable training data at lower cost than teleoperation.

2611.05609.t: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
2611.05609.s: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation can match in-distribution teacher performance while degrading out-of-distribution generalization, and geometry-based patching plus base-preserving replay can improve retention with limited in-distribution loss.

2610.41104.t: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation
2610.41104.s: Muon-RT reuses the EMA teacher-student displacement as momentum for hidden weight matrices, reducing persistent training memory while improving accuracy in self-distillation fine-tuning and policy optimization compared with AdamW and momentum Muon.

2611.06425.t: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
2611.06425.s: A standalone diffusion drafter using blockwise denoising and auxiliary autoregressive supervision enables asynchronous speculative decoding by drafting successor blocks during verification, yielding large decoding speedups.

2611.01120.t: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games
2611.01120.s: StreamDuo pairs a trainable commentator with a frozen research agent that retrieves game wiki entries to improve cross-game streaming commentary without training on target games.

2611.03852.t: Why Pay for Long Reasoning When Rewrite Do Trick? Causal Effects of Reasoning History Compaction on Future Generation and Agent Cost
2611.03852.s: Rewriting reasoning histories into compact state records reduces future reasoning length and token costs in open-weight models without retraining.

2611.01926.t: TAC-CoT: Tool-Empowered Implicit Chain-of-Thought via Interleaving Explicit Tokens
2611.01926.s: TAC-CoT replaces explicit chain-of-thought with compact latent reasoning while retaining text only for tool interactions, improving accuracy and reducing forward passes in agentic math and QA tasks.

2611.02846.t: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding
2611.02846.s: SpecOPD accelerates speculative decoding by parallelizing on-policy draft supervision across independent branches, improving acceptance length and training throughput across diverse model architectures and tasks.

2611.02857.t: Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver
2611.02857.s: Solv3R is a looped transformer that iteratively refines multi-view geometry from its current state, supporting offline, incremental, relocalization, and streaming reconstruction without task-specific training or modules.

2611.06768.t: PyRUA-REAL: Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning through RSI in the Real World
2611.06768.s: PyRUA-REAL enables coding agents to convert physical robot exploration into persistent executable skills, achieving high success rates across real-world and benchmark tasks through recursive self-improvement.

2611.03330.t: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference
2611.03330.s: A four-parameter analytical law predicts LLM inference energy across architectures, revealing quadratic prefill costs, GQA savings, and super-linear growth from reasoning budgets and agentic serving.

2611.06796.t: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation
2611.06796.s: Velocity Adversarial Distillation and its VA-TDM variant improve few-step diffusion and flow generation by using a learned critic and trajectory distribution matching to train efficient high-quality text-to-image and text-to-video generators.

2611.05648.t: NitroFusion2: Bringing Adversarial Loss to the Text Stream of Multimodal Diffusion Transformers
2611.05648.s: Text-Stream Adversarial Distillation and Aspect-Cued Discrimination use intermediate text-token states as a steerable adversarial representation to enable practical one- to two-step multimodal diffusion transformer generation.

2611.05304.t: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers
2611.05304.s: A novel vector quantization method for looped transformers addresses the memory bottleneck of the key-value cache by jointly encoding multiple loop steps, leading to substantial improvements in efficiency and maintaining high accuracy across various language modeling tasks.

2611.03404.t: VidDub: Replacement-Aware Distillation for Two-Step Video Dubbing
2611.03404.s: VidDub is a two-step diffusion video dubbing model that uses replacement-aware cross-audio supervision to avoid conflicting source-mouth targets and achieves strong lip synchronization with high visual fidelity.

2611.03768.t: Multi-layer Indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in DeepSeek Sparse Attention
2611.03768.s: A multi-layer indexer reuses adjacent layers' token selections to overlap indexer scans with attention, speeding up long-context decoding of sparse-attention LLMs without retraining or accuracy loss.

2611.06083.t: SleuthVLM: Do We Really Need Audio-in-Video for Omni Video Understanding?
2611.06083.s: A vision-language model agent that transcribes speech and reasons over video without direct audio input achieves state-of-the-art omni video understanding, indicating agentic ability matters more than audio perception or larger omni models.

2611.04760.t: Koopman Generative Operators for Efficient Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
2611.04760.s: KGO unifies structured latent dynamics with single-step flow matching and adaptive uncertainty gating to achieve accurate, efficient probabilistic time-series forecasting.

2611.03517.t: Ask, Don't Equip: Question-Driven Coding Agents for Deep Kernel Optimization
2611.03517.s: A question-driven LLM agent improves CUDA kernels by asking targeted questions at decision points, achieving faster FlashAttention implementations than a tool-rich autonomous baseline.

2611.03394.s: TaoMate-HD is an autoregressive streaming model that generates high-resolution audiovisual content in chunks with progressive denoising, history-based continuation, and optimized parallel deployment for faster, coherent long-form output.

2611.04949.t: HERIT: Enabling Global Access to Hanja-to-English Historical Translation by Mitigating Temporal Bias
2611.04949.s: HERIT adapts machine translation to historical archives via retrieval-augmented pseudo-labeling, improving accuracy across time periods and unlocking global access.

2611.05029.t: DRAP: Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity for Continual Learning in Physical AI
2611.05029.s: DRAP improves replay-free continual learning for physical AI by adaptively reducing plasticity of critical model components based on trajectory-amplification risk, enhancing retention of past behaviors without sacrificing new task learning.

2611.04916.t: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
2611.04916.s: Kling's multimodal understanding stack links caption density, perceptual text encoding, reward modeling, and evaluation protocols to improve controllable video generation.

2611.00617.t: Words Caught in the Heart: Simulating Person-Specific Expression for Self-Opaque Clients in Psychotherapy
2611.00617.s: Pandora is a psychotherapy client simulation framework that models evolving psychological and relational states to generate more authentic, individually aligned expressions and reduce AI-like responses.

2611.02737.t: MoviEdit: Long-form Multi-Shot Video Editing Made Easy
2611.02737.s: MoviEdit is an end-to-end framework for long-form multi-shot video editing that uses cascaded bidirectional-autoregressive modeling and a new benchmark to maintain coherence across scenes while reducing manual data annotation.

2611.05377.t: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
2611.05377.s: DreamX leverages a pretrained video diffusion model to learn compact, appearance-invariant latent actions that enable cross-embodiment transfer and efficient policy learning.

2611.02497.t: RoboColosseum: Evaluating Physical Intelligence at Scale In-The-Wild
2611.02497.s: RoboColosseum evaluates general robot policies across diverse embodiments and environments, revealing weak cross-embodiment agreement, limited open-world reliability, and substantial differences between zero-shot and fine-tuned performance.

2611.04814.t: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
2611.04814.s: LoCo uses local preference learning to teach reasoning models when to stop deliberating, reducing output length substantially while preserving or improving accuracy across math and code tasks.

2611.03233.t: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
2611.03233.s: Axion 1.0 is an open agent foundation model trained via a concise three-stage pipeline of supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, achieving competitive agentic performance while fully releasing its data and training recipe.

2611.05193.t: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval
2611.05193.s: FactEmbed improves composed image retrieval by decoupling query understanding from embedding construction through factorized latents that simulate visual modifications before retrieval.

2611.05280.t: YANAMI: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Multiturn Stateful Interaction
2611.05280.s: YANAMI introduces a large-scale multimodal dialogue dataset and benchmark for stateful interaction, requiring models to track and realize evolving dialogue states across turns, and reveals that current unified multimodal models still struggle with this task.

2610.39813.t: EvoTeam: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Teams
2610.39813.s: EvoTeam evolves multi-agent collaboration by jointly adapting team organization, interaction rules, and agent skills through execution experience while maintaining reusable team libraries.

2611.03634.t: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
2611.03634.s: WebHarbor provides 153 executable, dockerized web environments for stable evaluation and reinforcement learning training of GUI agents, enabling strong generalization across multi-step and post-authentication tasks.

2611.05306.s: Frequent context compaction preserves task accuracy across long-horizon and long-input tasks, suggesting that long-context language models may be unnecessary and motivating semantic state space models.

2610.40747.t: Mage-VL-Cowork: A Full Training Recipe to Learn Hybrid Computer Use From Evolved Harnesses
2610.40747.s: Mage-VL-Cowork is a 4B hybrid computer-use agent trained via a progressive curriculum and scalable synthetic data generation, achieving state-of-the-art performance on OSWorld-Verified with efficient reasoning.

2611.02079.t: ParetoSaddler: Pareto-Guided Optimization of Agent Harnesses for Quality and Cost
2611.02079.s: ParetoSaddler improves LLM agent harnesses by separately promoting intermediate candidates via Bayesian bootstrap Pareto support and selecting final deployments, boosting quality while reducing cost.

2611.02501.t: SpecPilot: Autonomous Algorithm Discovery and Systems Optimization for Speculative Decoding
2611.02501.s: SpecPilot autonomously discovers deployment-specific algorithms and system optimizations to maximize speculative decoding speedups across diverse models, drafters, and serving regimes without quality loss.

2611.04035.t: Recursa: Toward Recursively Self-Improving Foundation Model Systems
2611.04035.s: Recursa is a self-improving foundation model system that adapts to new domains by recursively learning from its own experience, storing skills and reflections in a knowledge repository, and validating improvements without human supervision or stronger teachers.
