2610.00854.t: Are Frontier VLM Agents Ready to Be Robot Generalists? An Empirical Study with the Embodied Agent Arena
2610.00854.s: Frontier vision-language models vary widely in embodied task performance, with closed-weight systems leading in planning and manipulation while open-weight models lag, and failure patterns reveal distinct geometric, control, and reasoning errors rather than uniform deficits.

2611.03998.s: Dory1.0-4B is a 4-billion-parameter recurrent language model with elastic depth that improves accuracy and token efficiency by looping a shared block, outperforming larger models on multiple benchmarks.

2610.40574.t: Every Token Needs Its Own Teacher: Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-distillation
2610.40574.s: Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-Distillation selects a preferred teacher for each token during training, improving mathematical reasoning performance over fixed-teacher methods.

2611.05163.t: RoboTryOn: Synthesizing Dexterous Robot Demonstrations from Human Videos via Virtual Try-On
2611.05163.s: RoboTryOn translates human demonstration videos into robot videos to train control policies without real robot demonstrations, improving success rates and reducing data collection costs.

2611.04303.t: FlowTranslator: Training-Free In-Image Machine Translation with Flow-Based Editing
2611.04303.s: FlowTranslator is a training-free framework for in-image machine translation that uses diffusion trajectory controls to generate accurate translated text within images without paired training data.

2611.05345.t: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
2611.05345.s: Speculative decoding can be trained to reject critical reasoning tokens so they are verified by the target model, reducing numerical noise and improving long-horizon agent accuracy without altering the target model.

2611.02017.t: Switch-SWE: Do Coding Agents Hold Focus When Switching Between Unfinished Tasks?
2611.02017.s: A benchmark for resuming interrupted software tasks reveals performance drops from interleaved work, and a context-management module improves recovery.

2611.03685.t: LOLPlay: Benchmarking Real-Time Visual Agents in League of Legends
2611.03685.s: LOLPlay evaluates visual agents on real-time League of Legends tasks, finding that increased reasoning effort does not improve success and can reduce interaction time.

2611.04449.t: Near-Zero Token Embeddings Silently Stall Training in Gated Sequence Models
2611.04449.s: Near-zero input embeddings in untied gated language models cause extreme gradient amplification and training instability, which is addressed by GroupClip and GateFloor remedies.

2610.37914.t: Muon Makes the First Mixture-of-Experts Layer Harder to Balance
2610.37914.s: Using Muon to train mixture-of-experts language models increases routing imbalance in early layers, which can be mitigated by centering router inputs or reducing the optimizer learning rate.

2611.04467.t: Is Forgetting Unified? Exploring Concept Unlearning in Unified Multimodal Models
2611.04467.o: Chinese Academic of Science Institute of Automation
2611.04467.s: Cross-pathway concept unlearning in unified multimodal models is addressed by a new benchmark and method that jointly suppresses target concept generation and recognition while preserving other capabilities.

2610.39251.t: Where to Learn and How Far to Roll Out: Efficient Adaptive Training for GUI Agents
2610.39251.s: A two-stage adaptive framework improves multi-step GUI agent training by using intermediate checkpoints and selective rollout ranges to reduce environment interactions while boosting performance.

2611.00352.s: Hidden-state reuse across factual questions partially transfers relation-specific answer shifts in small language models, with effectiveness depending on format, cohort, and source relation alignment.

2610.41366.t: What We Keep of What We Forget: Replacement Operators and Routing Semantics in Training-Free MoE Expert Pruning
2610.41366.s: Comparing replacement operators for pruned mixture-of-experts experts reveals that gate scaling and calibration domain strongly affect performance, with a proposed tilted novice operator improving results without dominating all settings.

2611.02476.t: GigaSpeech 3: Scaling Multi-Dialect Arabic Speech Recognition with Weakly Labeled Data
2611.02476.o: SJTU Cross Media Language Intelligence Lab
2611.02476.s: GigaSpeech 3 provides 39,000 hours of weakly transcribed dialectal Arabic speech, enabling improved recognition across five dialects via self-supervised labeling and noisy-student refinement.

2611.03747.t: Enhancing Stock Market Information Retrieval with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
2611.03747.s: A retrieval-augmented generation system for stock market queries improves response accuracy and speed, validated by high ROUGE scores and low latency.

2611.04414.t: SphereFlow: Missing Modality Imputation via Geometric Transport on Hypersphere
2611.04414.s: SphereFlow projects modalities onto a shared hypersphere to enable short-range cross-modal imputation via flow matching with geometry-aware noise and decoder modifications.

2611.04169.t: Length Is Cheap, Competition Is Not: Attention Predicts Context Rot in Retrieval
2611.04169.s: In retrieval tasks, language model failure on long inputs stems from attention competition rather than sequence length, as rival evidence statements sharply reduce accuracy while neutral filler does not.

2611.01860.s: This report proposes a unified taxonomy and literature system for agentic computer graphics driven by large language models, analyzing trends and open challenges in human-agent collaboration and long-horizon planning.

2611.00859.t: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
2611.00859.s: Wave Forcing enables efficient continuous long-video generation with consistent appearance and natural motion through co-designed generation, training, and execution, achieving high throughput and quality.

2611.03178.t: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
2611.03178.s: CoworkOS is a long-horizon agent harness that separates strategy from execution, supports human-in-the-loop collaboration via shared artifacts, and improves model performance through sustained automated post-training.

2610.40191.t: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
2610.40191.s: Agent harnesses integrate video generation and world models to enable planning, tool use, and recursive self-improvement for autonomous multi-shot video production.

2611.01560.t: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
2611.01560.s: Uni-robot-agent enables open-weight robot-use agents to surpass proprietary models in zero-shot manipulation and suggests joint development of four core capabilities for future training.

2611.02074.t: SWE-Trail: History-Guided Trajectory Collection for Coding Agent Training
2611.02074.s: SWE-Trail improves trajectory collection for coding agents by using past rollouts to guide exploration without exposing history to the agent, yielding better-trained student models.

2611.02897.t: PhotoGuider: Composition-Aware Cropping and 360^{circ} View Framing with Explainable Photographic Assessments
2611.02897.s: PhotoGuider selects viewing directions and frames 360° panoramas using shared composition-aware tokens and produces camera-parameter outputs with explanation-conditioned scoring.

2610.27954.t: Lost in Recovery: Demystifying Recovery Behavior of Computer-Use Agents via Goal-Oriented Action Replay
2610.27954.s: ReTrace is a framework that evaluates recovery behavior in computer-use agents by formalizing transition-consistent recovery and demonstrating that autonomous model-based recovery improves long-horizon reliability.

2611.02112.s: Order-only on-policy distillation trains students to match teacher token rankings rather than probabilities, improving reasoning performance without temperature tuning.

2611.02102.t: NorthCUA Technical Report: Turbocharging Computer-Use Agents through Experience at Scale
2611.02102.s: NorthCUA scales computer-use agents via an experience flywheel, recursive self-improvement, staged learning, and reinforcement learning to achieve state-of-the-art open-source GUI and web interaction results.

2611.01815.t: When Does Latent Prediction Error Support Physical Surprise Claims in Video World Models?
2611.01815.s: The study evaluates frozen video representations to show that prediction errors reflect appearance and motion rather than reliably measuring physical surprise.

2611.03602.t: Reviso: Not All Visual Evidence Deserves Equal Attention in Video Captioning
2611.03602.s: Reviso is an agentic video captioning framework that learns to prioritize key visual evidence through hierarchical planning and active perception, improving caption quality and downstream video understanding.

2611.00172.t: From Fragmentation to Fusion: A Survey and Roadmap for Omnimodal Embeddings
2611.00172.s: Embedding research across modalities is converging toward shared principles via contrastive learning and Transformers, and a framework of coverage, comparability, and compositionality is proposed to unify it through transformation, alignment, and joint embedding.

2611.03344.t: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell
2611.03344.s: FLAMIA accelerates Transformer attention on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs via MXFP8 and mixed-precision kernels that reduce quantization overhead, prevent causal leakage, and support variable-length packed documents.

2611.02782.t: History Forcing: Distilling History-Dependent Continuations for Long-Horizon Video World Models
2611.02782.s: History Forcing improves long-range consistency in few-step autoregressive video generation by using historical context residuals to correct distillation targets.

2610.39419.t: Diagnosing the Reference Gap: What Visual Scaffolds Can and Cannot Fix in Multimodal Reasoning
2610.39419.s: Multimodal language models fail at multi-step visual reasoning due to a reference gap rather than perception, and task-matched external references like numbering significantly improve accuracy without training.

2610.42128.t: DecisionRank: On-Policy Distillation for Decision-Model Rerankers
2610.42128.s: DecisionRank uses item-space on-policy distillation to transfer ranking knowledge from generative teachers to efficient decision models, achieving state-of-the-art retrieval performance with significantly faster inference.

2610.37826.t: DeFT-RAG: Decomposing Multi-Hop Questions into Self-Contained Sub-Questions with Reusable Answers
2610.37826.s: DeFT-RAG improves multi-hop question answering by generating self-contained sub-questions sequentially, offloading reasoning to rule-based updates and a lightweight decision model, and caching answers to reduce LLM usage.

2611.02332.t: LEANGUARD: Lean-Verified Guardrails for Tool-Using Agents
2611.02332.s: LeanGuard is a verified runtime that blocks policy-violating tool calls by language-model agents and can repair them via proof-guided search, reducing unauthorized executions and prompt-injection success without harming benign task performance.

2611.03526.t: Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime
2611.03526.s: Library of Layers dynamically orders transformer blocks during inference to adapt computation to tasks, enabling parameter reuse, sparsity, and interpretable routing across reasoning, multilingual, and safety settings.

2610.41574.t: BYOD: Build Your Own DLM - Efficient Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Language Model Conversion
2610.41574.s: BYOD converts autoregressive language models into diffusion models via parameter-efficient LoRA adapters, enabling parallel generation with minimal training cost while preserving base-model knowledge.

2610.40293.t: MAServeBench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent LLM Serving Systems with Hierarchical Collaboration Workloads
2610.40293.s: MAServeBench evaluates LLM serving and hardware by modeling multi-agent collaboration as a configurable workload dimension with reproducible dependency traces.

2610.41296.t: Self-Improvement with Auxiliary Rewards: Learning from Verified Traces and Evaluating Transfer
2610.41296.s: Auxiliary trajectory preferences based on entropy and confidence metrics improve small language model self-improvement and transfer by distinguishing learning value among equally correct reasoning traces.

2610.27815.s: ProVe reverses speculative decoding roles by fine-tuning a large model to propose token blocks and verifying them with a smaller or identical model, achieving faster autoregressive generation with adjustable speed-accuracy tradeoffs.

2611.03097.t: DR Pixel: Page-Native Deep Research with Vision-Language Models
2611.03097.s: DR Pixel is an open-source multimodal agent that performs deep research directly on rendered document page images, improving retrieval and reasoning over scientific papers through counterfactual credit reweighting.

2611.03219.t: Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?
2611.03219.s: Empirical study shows continual harness self-evolution across software engineering tasks causes severe catastrophic forgetting, with performance on earlier datasets dropping sharply after later evolution.

2610.38637.s: Teacher-Evolution Self-Distillation improves on-policy self-distillation by continuously enhancing self-teaching reliability through reward-guided teacher optimization and adaptive down-weighting of unreliable samples.

2610.39639.t: Where Do Vision Language Models Fail at 3D Reasoning?
2610.39639.s: Vision-language models often judge 3D object properties correctly but fail to recover and consistently apply exact per-color counts, motivating evaluation by exact correctness, consistency, and visual dependence.

2610.38252.t: A Tutorial on Generative Models for Music Audio
2610.38252.s: This monograph surveys neural methods for music audio generation, covering codecs, autoregressive and diffusion models, flow matching, preference optimization, evaluation practices, and legal considerations.

2611.00053.t: SIMIT: Self-Improving Vision-Language Models via Imagination at Test-Time
2611.00053.s: SIMIT is a test-time framework that lets vision-language models generate their own practice data to improve answers on unlabeled queries without external annotations.

2610.39278.t: WorldFlow: Joint Video and 3D Motion Prediction via Large-Scale Pretraining
2610.39278.s: WorldFlow is a generative world model that jointly predicts future video and 3D trajectories using continuous displacement tokens and a Mixture-of-Transformers backbone, improving physical dynamics prediction across diverse benchmarks.

2611.02928.t: Lab2Sim: Turning Real-World Experiment Videos into Interactive Virtual Experiments
2611.02928.s: Lab2Sim introduces a benchmark for converting science videos into interactive virtual experiments, and EduVideo2Code improves apparatus fidelity by encoding procedures as state machines for verified code generation.

2610.41994.t: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention
2610.41994.s: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization improves long-context retrieval in gated linear recurrent models by jointly configuring decay and sensitivity parameters before training.

2610.42149.t: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
2610.42149.s: LARC enables continuous latent reasoning for unified multimodal models, improving image generation quality and enabling test-time scaling without discrete token bottlenecks.

2610.40738.t: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use
2610.40738.s: Apriel Voice 27B Preview is an open speech-language model that integrates speech understanding, reasoning, and tool use within a shared backbone, achieving strong results on audio benchmarks through a two-stage training procedure with online distillation.

2610.36545.t: FrameForge: Harnessing Priors of Video Foundation Models for Unified Image Generation
2610.36545.s: FrameForge enables adaptive conditional image generation by modeling variable condition-target relationships through dynamic temporal experts and intermediate reasoning pathways in pretrained video models.

2610.42136.t: ReLift: Dense 3D Tracking as Lifted Trajectory Repair
2610.42136.s: ReLift improves dense 3D tracking by repairing and completing lifted trajectories using geometric trajectory refinement without requiring image-based training.

2610.34722.t: CEPO: A General Framework for Improving Prompt Optimization in Multi-Agent Systems
2610.34722.s: CEPO improves multi-agent prompt optimization by separating shared coordination from agent-specific execution, boosting performance across benchmarks and scaling efficiently with more agents.

2610.40339.t: Wizard: Manipulate Any World in Real Time via Agentic Control
2610.40339.s: Wizard is an agentic game world model that uses structured motion proxies and adaptive masking to enable real-time, generalizable video generation with precise character control across diverse scenes.

2610.37918.t: Venus-DefakerOne2: A Vision-Forensics Foundation Model with Broader Coverage
2610.37918.s: Venus-DefakerOne2 is a unified anti-forgery foundation model that extends detection to diverse forgery forms and media types through alternating LoRA and full-parameter tuning and entropy-based test adaptation.

2610.40799.t: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
2610.40799.s: CaPtain trains small open vision-language models via supervised fine-tuning and multi-turn reinforcement learning with a physical critic to perform robot manipulation through code, achieving strong results without frontier models or vision-language-action backbones.

2610.40373.t: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model
2610.40373.s: HiFOR improves robotic manipulation by hierarchically predicting future states and retrieving relevant future information to guide action generation.

2610.42053.t: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
2610.42053.s: REA unifies deliberative and reactive policies in a single runtime with asynchronous coordination, achieving high success rates with reduced control overhead across simulated and real robot tasks.

2610.40748.t: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
2610.40748.s: WorldBridge improves robot task generalization by combining video prediction with sparse action supervision via separate video and action experts, achieving state-of-the-art results across manipulation benchmarks.

2610.36384.t: SOMA: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Egocentric Behavior and Body-Motion Understanding
2610.36384.s: SOMA is a benchmark assessing fine-grained egocentric body-motion reasoning in multimodal models, revealing substantial gaps versus human performance and providing training data and a multimodal baseline to advance the field.

2610.39276.t: MemSteer: Turning User Histories into Supervision for Agent Memory Optimization
2610.39276.s: MemSteer generates evidence-grounded QA supervision from unlabeled user histories to optimize agent memory design without model updates, improving benchmark scores significantly.

2610.35850.t: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
2610.35850.s: OSWAM enables real-time, high-quality action generation in autonomous driving and embodied control by initializing diffusion with structured imagination tokens and distilling future-conditioned privileged information into a single denoising step.

2610.40945.t: On the Origin and Evolution of Training-Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning
2610.40945.s: On-policy reinforcement learning for large language models suffers from training-inference mismatch due to numerical discrepancies and policy lag, and a derived discrepancy-lag correction stabilizes training by centering errors, clipping importance ratios, and resynchronizing sampling.

2610.42141.t: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
2610.42141.s: RoboArchitect automates robot harness design by iteratively revising control code around a frozen policy, substantially improving success on unseen scenes and tasks without model updates.

2610.40914.t: No Channels Left Behind: Understanding Diffusion Acceleration through Residual Gates
2610.40914.s: Training acceleration in diffusion transformers is driven by reorganization of AdaLN-Zero residual gates, and a simple radial objective promoting broader gate participation improves generation quality without auxiliary teachers.

2610.37903.t: Think Twice: The Metis-1.6 Technical Report
2610.37903.s: Metis-1.6 introduces small, efficient mixture-of-experts language models trained with limited data that achieve competitive math performance and Pareto-optimal efficiency despite training errors and architectural issues.

2610.42096.t: CausalWAM: Learning the Causes of Actions in World Action Models
2610.42096.s: Causal World Action Models enforce sparse routing to isolate action-relevant latent variables, ensuring identifiable causal structure without requiring temporal independence assumptions.

2610.16927.t: WeFair: Fidelity-Aware Alignment from Human Feedback for Personalized Query Rewriting in Short-Video Search
2610.16927.s: WeFair improves personalized query rewriting via fidelity-aware human feedback stages—demonstration, preference, and verification—to reduce intent drift and boost search effectiveness in short-video platforms.

2610.41260.t: SketchDirector: Complex Scene Sketching via Agentic Layout Reasoning and Detail Refinement
2610.41260.o: GVC Lab at Great Bay University
2610.41260.s: SketchDirector is an agentic framework that decomposes text prompts into draft vector assets, arranges them via iterative reasoning with self-evolving memory, and refines details using diffusion priors for complex scene sketching.

2610.36671.t: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
2610.36671.s: LOWN adaptively skips image processing during diffusion vision-language model decoding when predictions agree, reducing computation while preserving accuracy.

2610.39302.t: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
2610.39302.s: Joint-embedding predictive architectures trained on aligned multi-modal observations converge to shared representations with far greater efficiency than next-token prediction, demonstrating that positive view design—not scale alone—drives cross-modal alignment.

2610.38568.t: A-RSI: Adaptive Task Refresh for Zero-Data Multimodal Self-Improvement
2610.38568.s: A-RSI improves recursive self-improvement by refreshing training tasks based on declining learning signals and using independently verifiable program-generated answers, raising benchmark performance without external labels.

2610.40614.t: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory
2610.40614.s: L3G-World uses a compact latent 3D Gaussian memory and alternating autoregressive updates with a video diffusion transformer to generate spatially consistent interactive worlds in real time.

2610.37161.t: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training
2610.37161.s: WorkFactory builds coherent professional tasks via information planning and repair, yielding WorkPilot models that improve expert-level agent performance across benchmarks.

2610.32411.t: A Broader Look into MLLM's Retrieval Heads
2610.32411.s: Retrieval heads remain sparse and shared across audio-visual modalities, and optimizing them improves document retrieval performance in multimodal models.

2610.39633.s: Intrinsic Distribution Matching improves few-step text-to-image generation by adding explicit moment constraints to distribution matching distillation, achieving state-of-the-art long-text rendering with minimal network evaluations.

2610.33106.t: VibeGame: Prompt-to-Game Development with AI-Native Engine and Self-Evolving Adversarial Agent Team
2610.33106.s: VibeGame is a framework that uses specialized adversarial agents and an AI-native engine to build complete 2D games from natural-language prompts with interactive validation and self-evolving reusable components.

2610.38331.s: Soft-MTP removes a noisy gradient residual from multi-token prediction via a straight-through KL recovery trick, improving perplexity, speculative decoding, and reasoning without added cost.

2610.38352.t: WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video
2610.38352.s: WeVisCut is a script-to-video system that trains a compact policy to coordinate video editing tools, recover from failures, and reduce token usage while maintaining quality.

2610.40647.t: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
2610.40647.s: SpecSlot improves pixel-space generative Transformers by using localized spectral slots and restricted global attention to increase image detail without raising computational cost.

2610.37786.t: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
2610.37786.s: WebAnything automates the reconstruction of reusable, source-grounded web environments from real URLs, enabling scalable agent training and evaluation with verified fidelity.

2610.39301.t: Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities
2610.39301.s: Youtu-Parsing-Omni is a unified multi-modal parser that encodes documents, images, audio, and video into structured spatiotemporal records using shared weights and cross-modal fusion, achieving state-of-the-art results across parsing benchmarks through a self-evolving on-policy distillation procedure.

2610.38425.t: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation
2610.38425.s: IntReal introduces a real-world interleaved multimodal dataset and evaluation framework to diagnose unified model strengths and improve generation through targeted training.

2610.40564.t: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
2610.40564.s: Foundation-model training stages can be unified under a single likelihood-based algorithm that blends static data and reinforcement learning generations, improving efficiency and capability retention.

2610.40454.t: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker
2610.40454.s: Glance integrates reranking and generation into a single backbone using lightweight adapters and pointer heads to score passages from shared context, reducing memory overhead while improving retrieval and answer quality.

2610.39664.s: EditAgent broadens agentic image editing by routing steps to diverse editors and using verification records for listwise judging, improving reliability and efficiency.

2610.39264.t: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps
2610.39264.s: An online reinforcement learning framework trains UI navigation agents on live mobile apps using a planning agent, UI grounding model, and a novel neighbor-conditioned value estimation method to improve robustness and reduce inference costs.

2610.38678.t: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding
2610.38678.o: Chinese Academic of Science Institute of Automation
2610.38678.s: Proactive video understanding should include asking for missing information under uncertainty, and the AskStream benchmark reveals current models struggle with this decision.

2610.40362.t: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training
2610.40362.s: Effective learning rate trajectories primarily drive weight-normalized training gains, motivating an affine inverse-square-root schedule that improves large-scale pretraining loss and robustness.

2609.05881.t: Broken on Arrival: Non-Functional Quantized LLM Artifacts in Public Model Registries and How to Catch Them
2609.05881.s: Quantized small language model files in public registries can be non-functional due to uncalibrated quantization recipes, and screening plus calibration is recommended before release.

2610.39287.t: OpenFlyV2: An onboard vision-language-action model for aerial perception and navigation
2610.39287.s: OpenFlyV2 is a unified onboard vision-language-action model that enables real-time aerial navigation and reasoning on resource-constrained hardware using shared multimodal representations.

2610.39663.t: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers
2610.39663.s: AB-Attention approximates dense video diffusion attention with high sparsity via intra-block clustering, weighted sampling, and fine-grained kernel gathering, improving fidelity and speed.

2610.25276.t: Holo4D: Holistic 4D Reconstruction as Geometric Control for Video Diffusion
2610.25276.s: Holo4D guides video diffusion with reconstructed 3D trajectory scaffolds to synthesize novel-view videos while preserving geometry and motion.

2610.36420.s: A simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation on low-cost robot arms reveals that hybrid LLM agents outperform learned vision-language-action policies, with ranking consistency between simulation and real hardware.

2610.23656.t: ABF-Bench: A Verifiable Benchmark for Agentic Blockchain Forensics
2610.23656.s: ABF-Bench introduces an interactive, evidence-backed benchmark for blockchain fund tracing that evaluates adaptive agents against fixed tracers, revealing gaps in recall and overconfidence while enabling verifiable LLM agent training.

2610.38681.t: Weaken to Strengthen: Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
2610.38681.s: WISD improves reasoning models by contrasting them with weaker quantized or pruned versions to generate training signals without privileged data.

2610.39293.t: Unlocking Any-Order Generation in Pretrained Autoregressive Image Models
2610.39293.s: Pretrained raster-scan autoregressive image models can be adapted into flexible any-order generators via future-aware positional embeddings and an ordering curriculum, enabling inpainting and outpainting with minimal extra compute.

2610.35684.t: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images
2610.35684.s: OmniShowcase improves subject-to-video generation by using geometry-driven training data and surface-normal conditioning to maintain 3D consistency across novel viewpoints.

2610.37230.t: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving
2610.37230.s: TAO improves scheduling for LLM agent services by considering tool readiness and using dynamic programming to place sessions, reducing latency and increasing throughput.

2610.22990.t: PersonaCUABench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents Serving Diverse Personas
2610.22990.s: PersonaCUABench reveals that computer-use agents frequently fail to satisfy real user requirements and constraints, reducing task completion and satisfaction compared to fixed benchmark instructions.

2610.20832.t: Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs
2610.20832.s: Large language models learn adaptive information gathering by training reasoning with information-gain rewards, improving experimental design efficiency and generalizing across tasks.

2610.30132.t: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
2610.30132.s: LongZero enables large language models to self-improve long-context reasoning by synthesizing structured multi-hop and retrieval tasks and training with GRPO without external data.

2610.35671.t: Evaluating DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks
2610.35671.s: Independent safety evaluation of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 reveals substantial improvements over prior versions and near-parity with leading closed-source models, while recommending process-level observability, incremental safety testing, and private benchmarks.

2610.31670.t: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
2610.31670.s: Sensorimotor alignment measures how sensory representations match physical motion geometry, serving as a low-cost offline predictor of robot model performance.

2610.27100.t: LOB-Impact Benchmark: Emergent Market Impact in Generative Limit Order Book Models
2610.27100.s: Neural generative limit order book models trained for next-token prediction exhibit emergent market impact under metaorder injection, though relaxation decay remains unobserved due to limited context windows.

2610.34186.t: HuGe: Scaling Humanoid Generalist Vision-Language-Action Models with Egocentric Experience
2610.34186.s: HuGe pre-trains vision-language-action models on egocentric human and robot data with pseudo-proprioception and visual adaptation to enable whole-body humanoid control.

2610.37626.t: Know, then Draw: A New Learning Paradigm for Visual Generation
2610.37626.s: A hybrid paradigm combining autoregressive pretraining for semantics and diffusion post-training for rendering achieves efficient, high-quality text-to-image generation with favorable scaling laws.

2610.37381.t: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
2610.37381.s: PDRVLA improves robot action generation by integrating a lightweight physical dynamics module that predicts future visual features with world-model supervision, avoiding online video generation latency.

2610.36729.t: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
2610.36729.s: Hy-Nomas is a video world model that uses causal attention and structured conditioning to generate interactive, multi-turn video segments with text and camera control.

2610.37666.t: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
2610.37666.s: ThinkWorld improves robotic generalization by representing actions as dynamics chains and using world imagination to learn from unlabeled human videos.

2610.36068.t: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
2610.36068.s: Rollback improves robot policies by using world models to rewind to past decisions, explore counterfactual actions, and generate fine-grained supervision, while continuously refining dynamics via real-world feedback.

2610.36077.t: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
2610.36077.s: The Trinity framework recursively improves multimodal agents by organizing tasks into a capability tree, generating simulated training worlds, and routing specialized harness modules to boost performance on diverse benchmarks.

2610.37341.t: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?
2610.37341.s: Executable code representations of video content improve reasoning and reconstruction over natural language, yet current multimodal models still struggle to generate faithful code captions for complex temporal dynamics.

2610.36456.t: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization
2610.36456.s: LociArt enables precise local video stylization with region-style control and temporal consistency via a generative refinement network, automated dataset construction, and a dedicated benchmark.

2610.24520.t: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory
2610.24520.s: HABIT-Bench evaluates whether LLM agent memory systems can infer implicit user habits from sparse dialogue evidence and apply them correctly across long-term interactions.

2610.37662.t: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
2610.37662.s: Factorized Vector Quantization improves discrete visual token quality by using parallel codebooks on complementary feature views, enabling discrete representations to match continuous ones in multimodal understanding.

2610.37037.t: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
2610.37037.s: EvidenceConnect synthesizes training data to strengthen visual evidence connection, improving spatial perception and multimodal reasoning across diverse tasks.

2610.34073.t: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
2610.34073.s: Large-scale evaluation reveals that dedicated memory systems often underperform naive retrieval-augmented generation, introducing a framework of memory benefit and memory tax to assess net value.

2610.33624.t: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback
2610.33624.s: RSI Arena demonstrates that autonomous AI agents can independently train and iteratively improve language models using human feedback, with most agents achieving preference gains in a second stage despite modest benchmark improvements.

2610.35962.t: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
2610.35962.s: A simple agentic loop with efficient Lean feedback achieves state-of-the-art formal theorem proving without structured workflows, showing that execution interfaces matter more than complex orchestration.

2610.35864.t: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
2610.35864.s: VibeVideoBench evaluates multimodal agents that generate videos via code, finding that top systems meet core requirements on most tasks but frequently fail due to poor time management.

2610.37386.t: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data
2610.37386.s: Prox replaces calibrated thresholds with top-k channel selection and a weight-derived reader to accelerate Mixture-of-Experts inference while preserving accuracy.

2610.34491.t: What Effort Level Should I Choose? On the Economics of Reasoning Effort in LLM Agents
2610.34491.s: Reasoning effort in generative models acts as a credence good where higher compute does not guarantee better instance-level results, and an escalation strategy from low effort improves cost-efficiency.

2610.35439.t: Omni-InteractScope: Benchmarking Proactive and Agentic Interaction in Continuous Omnimodal Streams
2610.35439.s: Omni-InteractScope evaluates continuous audiovisual interaction reliability, revealing that current Omni-LLMs struggle with timely tool use, query-free reminders, and sustained guidance.

2610.32046.t: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?
2610.32046.s: Test-Time Memory Evolution updates external memory without changing model weights to guide scientific discovery more efficiently than test-time training.

2610.34724.t: Harness-Model Collaboration for Long-Horizon Continual Learning
2610.34724.s: HaMo combines rapid retrieval of procedural experience cards with gradual model adaptation to improve long-horizon web agents' retention and cross-task execution.

2610.36466.t: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni: Elastic Self-Refining Unified Diffusion LLM with Cross-Paradigm On-Policy Distillation
2610.36466.s: NLD-Uni is a unified discrete diffusion language model that combines visual understanding and generation via cross-paradigm on-policy distillation and progressive self-refining diffusion.

2610.22543.t: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
2610.22543.s: SPOT accelerates diffusion language models by predicting token generation order and verifying candidates in parallel, reducing passes up to 6.8x while maintaining exact decoding.

2610.34674.t: Benchmarking Obstacle-Conditioned Safety in Household Robot Navigation
2610.34674.s: The study introduces a benchmark and metric to evaluate whether robot navigation policies adapt continuous motion to obstacle safety semantics, revealing a gap in translating semantic caution into safe movement.

2610.36791.t: RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions
2610.36791.s: RynnWorld-Latent learns cross-embodiment world dynamics via 3D-grounded latent actions, enabling joint pretraining on diverse video sources and synthetic data generation for improved robot policy performance.

2610.36269.t: Cross-modal Steering Vectors Exist Across Both Image and Text Generation
2610.36269.s: Cross-modal steering vectors transfer between text and image generation in unified multimodal models, revealing shared causal control mechanisms despite a modality gap.

2610.26030.t: Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation
2610.26030.s: Looped transformers trained with full backpropagation through time outperform truncated alternatives under matched compute, with scaling laws identifying two loops as optimal when model size is adjustable.

2610.33066.s: OvisOCR3 is a compact 0.8B vision-language model that unifies diverse OCR tasks through multi-teacher distillation and reinforcement learning, achieving state-of-the-art results across document parsing, general OCR, key information extraction, figure captioning, and cross-page table reconstruction.

2610.30435.t: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
2610.30435.s: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning trains search agents to recognize missing information and improve search efficiency without extra inference-time assessment.

2610.37175.t: MLE-World: Predicting Machine Learning Experiment Outcomes with a Learned World Model
2610.37175.s: A world model predicts machine learning program outcomes to enable affordable test-time scaling for AI research agents, improving performance with fewer real executions.

2610.37219.t: Vision-Language-Action or World-Action? Just Action Models
2610.37219.s: Just Action Model decouples backbone initialization, future observation objectives, and inference machinery to improve robot control with foresight training and reduced computation.

2610.36082.t: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning
2610.36082.s: Fin-SD improves local multi-step financial reasoning by using self-generated error critiques and truncated correct prefixes for on-policy distillation without external teachers.

2610.22684.t: AlphaBet: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Event Forecasting Agents
2610.22684.s: AlphaBet uses agentic reinforcement learning to train a single LLM policy to search, reason, and report forecast probabilities across multiple dates, reducing Brier scores by improving both evidence acquisition and probability reporting.

2610.36192.t: Beyond the Estimate: Wiener-Informed Decoding for Easier Training of Pixel-Space Flow Models
2610.36192.s: Wiener-informed Decoding accelerates pixel-space velocity model training and improves image generation by integrating statistical predictions into decoder computation without altering native blocks.

2610.29003.t: T-DIG: Text-Conditioned Diversity for Image Generation
2610.29003.s: T-DIG is a text-conditioned diversity framework that uses an LLM policy with reinforcement learning to generate axis-specific image variations via frozen generators, enabling user-directed exploration without model retraining.

2610.35845.t: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
2610.35845.s: The paper proposes a unified framework for work agents that integrates foundation models with runtime harnesses to execute complex digital tasks reliably, introducing dimensions of persistence and openness alongside capability families and evaluation metrics.

2610.34662.t: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
2610.34662.s: StreamVibe introduces a benchmark, streaming vision-language model, and hierarchical memory harness to enable proactive, intent-aware interaction with implicit and evolving user goals.

2610.33966.t: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
2610.33966.s: InteractiveWorld provides a verifiable simulation environment and benchmark to evaluate whether multimodal language models can reliably guide humans through physical tasks.

2610.34415.t: Spatial Audio Generation and Editing with Executable Plans and Self-Distilling Transfusion
2610.34415.s: AMBIT is a unified framework that generates and edits first-order ambisonics audio by coupling autoregressive scene planning with rectified-flow rendering, using a specialized continuous VAE and on-policy self-distillation to preserve spatial structure and acoustic fidelity.

2610.33135.t: WorldCast: World-Consistent Character Video Generation with Large-Angle Camera Control
2610.33135.s: CLACT and WorldCast enable consistent character video generation under large-angle camera motions by combining 3D point-cloud guidance with geometry-aligned memory attention.

2610.34467.s: DynaFlow enables adaptive multi-agent collaboration by letting a main agent synthesize executable workflows that coordinate sub-agents through structured execution and verification.

2610.33956.t: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
2610.33956.s: A new benchmark evaluates whether LLM agents improve through repeated professional tasks with feedback, revealing limited sustained learning in current frontier models.

2610.32285.t: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution
2610.32285.s: TraceTrial-Bench evaluates agent harness reliability across seven components using mechanism-oriented tasks, trajectory tracing, and failure attribution to compare harness designs and diagnose failures.

2610.33568.t: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
2610.33568.s: Trajectory2Gym constructs grounded, compositionally covered tool-use interactions and applies parent-normalized supervised fine-tuning, improving tool-use agent performance across Qwen3 scales on Tau1, Tau2, and BFCL.

2610.35193.t: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
2610.35193.s: This survey defines recursive self-improvement and organizes trustworthy advancement requirements into improvement validity, constraint preservation, and oversight across recursive update stages.

2610.33472.t: Qwen-Image-PE: Learning Visual Design for Text-to-Image Prompt Enhancement
2610.33472.s: Qwen-Image-PE improves text-to-image prompts via two-stage training with caption-based reverse distillation and groupwise design rewards, scaling across data, model size, and information density.

2610.33024.t: Evolving to Match Capabilities: Improving Harness Self-Evolution via Skill Adaptation
2610.33024.o: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
2610.33024.s: Harness self-evolution improves LLM agents via skill adaptation guided by a meta-skill that reformulates guidance to match executor capabilities, boosting weak models without parameter updates.

2610.33845.t: Build, Don't Play: Self-Improving LLM Research Agents Develop a Hearthstone Battlegrounds AI That Rivals Top Players
2610.33845.s: AutoTavern demonstrates that self-improving LLM research agents can autonomously build a faithful game simulator and train a reinforcement learning agent that surpasses top human players in Hearthstone Battlegrounds.

2610.35518.t: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
2610.35518.s: S3AC introduces a stabilized actor-critic training method with difficulty-aware prompt sampling to improve long reasoning in large language models without relying on grouped rollouts.

2610.19025.t: How Far Can Coding Agents Go in Visual Generation?
2610.19025.s: Coding agents build images via executable programs, showing structured visual reasoning and consistent internal scene representations across drawing interfaces.

2610.18683.t: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
2610.18683.s: ProAS improves credit assignment in critic-free reinforcement learning for LLM agents by using a dynamic reference graph to mask unreasonable incentives and redistribute penalties asymmetrically, boosting success rates and convergence speed.

2610.23928.t: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning
2610.23928.s: MiniTE enables stable low-bit reinforcement learning for large language models by aligning cross-engine numerical execution and accelerating native 4-bit computation.

2610.34735.t: iPrefBench: A User-Centric Benchmark for Personalized Mobile Use Agents
2610.34735.s: The study introduces iPrefBench, a benchmark for assessing whether mobile agents can infer missing user preferences from activity history or ask for necessary clarification, revealing that current agents execute actions well but fail at personalization.

2610.29915.t: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
2610.29915.s: CausalAlign improves long-horizon camera ego-motion consistency in diffusion video generators by aligning internal representations to 3D dynamics via delta-token space.

2610.31309.t: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization
2610.31309.s: OPTIC achieves extreme compression of per-layer embeddings by using token-shared indexed codes and layer-specific affine decoders fitted to the output path, preserving most model performance at up to 1000x compression with minimal inference overhead.

2610.34386.t: ParetoRSI-Gym: Can AI Agents Improve Language Models Across Multiple Domains?
2610.34386.s: ParetoRSI-Gym evaluates recursive self-improvement agents across multiple domains by fixing the model and pipeline while allowing data curation and training loops, revealing significant generalization gains and distinct agent strategies.

2610.34356.t: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
2610.34356.s: RynnVLA-Latent leverages latent actions derived from diverse video to pretrain large vision-language-action policies, achieving high success across simulated and real-world robot benchmarks without embodiment-specific tuning.

2610.31818.t: Nested Sparsity for Scalable Pretraining and Continual Learning
2610.31818.s: Nestor introduces nested sparsity in attention to improve conditional computation over standard mixture-of-experts transformers, enhancing pretraining, long-context adaptation, and continual learning.

2610.21240.s: Sparse autoencoders decompose language model activations into sparse features, and the redistribution sensitivity score identifies recurring feature changes that contribute to downstream readout failures without equating representation change with failure.

2610.34577.s: Verification strategies for agent harnesses—spanning instructions, reminders, gates, and independent review—show that independent critic review improves accuracy with minimal cost increases, guiding practical test-time scaling design.

2610.34241.t: Beyond Benchmarks: Can Small Open-Weight Models Get Real Coding Work Done?
2610.34241.s: Empirical studies of open-weight coding agents reveal that verified code success depends on serving setup, protocol design, and hidden behavioral checks rather than text coherence alone.

2610.33718.t: RoboJev: An Open Vision-Language Judge for Robot Success Detection
2610.33718.s: RoboJev-27B is an open-weight vision-language model that predicts robot manipulation success from video frames using LoRA fine-tuning, calibrated token readouts, and source-specific regularization, achieving high accuracy and generalization across labs and robots.

2610.14018.t: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Action Models
2610.14018.s: RoboHarness enables LLM agents to perform embodied manipulation via a visual-geometric control interface, surpassing specialized vision-language-action models on robotics benchmarks.

2610.29139.t: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
2610.29139.s: PAWM selectively predicts multi-step failures to guide black-box LLM agents away from pitfalls, improving performance via supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement co-training.

2610.33817.t: EnvLunch: The Environment as a Free Lunch for Learning to Interact
2610.33817.s: EnvLunch leverages executable environments to generate verifiable training trajectories without human annotations, improving agent performance and reducing labeled data requirements for downstream tasks.

2610.24451.t: Assessing the CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models: A Case Study of GPT-6 Astra
2610.24451.s: GPT-6 Astra demonstrates partial capability across CAD workflows but remains limited by geometric validity, parametric dependencies, and assembly errors.

2610.33877.t: Semantic Concept Steering Breaks the Explanation Drift Loop in Continual Learning
2610.33877.s: C3L prevents explanation drift in continual learning by anchoring saliency regularization to offline-discovered semantic concepts, suppressing spurious correlations through a relevance crowding-out effect.

2610.33732.t: Trust Mechanisms for Offline Generative AI at the Edge: A Connectivity-Regime Framework and an Empirical Study on a Raspberry Pi 5
2610.33732.s: Local retrieval-augmented generation on edge devices using signed knowledge packs and output validators improves efficiency but remains vulnerable to poisoned updates and cannot guarantee evidence truth.

2610.32177.t: Ψ-0.6: Adaptive Streams of Thought in a Unified Vision-Language World Model
2610.32177.s: A unified vision-language world model adaptively combines perception, language, geometry, and simulation through interleaved reasoning streams to improve spatial reasoning and counterfactual simulation.

2610.28490.t: Learning from Automatic 3D Gaussian Splatting Edits for Online Bayesian Scene Change Detection
2610.28490.s: The method learns scene-specific evidence models and priors from automatically edited 3D Gaussian Splatting representations to perform efficient online change detection via Bayesian fusion and object-guided refinement.

2610.31162.t: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
2610.31162.s: HiSTEVE is a hierarchical vision-language-action agent that combines long-horizon planning with native keyboard-and-mouse control to perform complex open-ended tasks in Minecraft.

2610.32965.s: RynnUnify is a 16B unified embodied model that integrates visual planning, physical reasoning, and robot control, achieving state-of-the-art results on long-horizon embodied tasks.

2610.31668.t: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
2610.31668.s: This survey unifies video understanding and generation through world modeling, organizing progress around inferring, synthesizing, sharing, and interacting with latent temporal states to emphasize persistent dynamics over clip-level perception.

2610.32770.t: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
2610.32770.s: Foundation models can self-improve across text and vision tasks by generating synthetic questions and reasoning traces guided only by high-level topics, without external supervision.

2610.19687.t: Function-Space Temporal Self-Distillation for Policy Optimization
2610.19687.s: Function-Space Policy Optimization improves reasoning and tool-use accuracy by combining temporal consolidation with privileged adaptation, reducing memory use and outperforming baselines.

2610.31066.t: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
2610.31066.s: Dual Exam evaluates multimodal agents and world models separately across diverse domains, revealing uneven performance and no coupled success in pilot tests.

2610.31931.t: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions
2610.31931.o: Lab of Efficient AI and Data
2610.31931.s: TWIG represents neural network weights as shared discrete decision paths, unifying compression methods and enabling efficient fixed-weight circuits with optimized discrete choices.

2610.27103.t: Omni-Woodpecker: Hallucination Correction via Evidence-Prior Rebalancing for Omni LLMs
2610.27103.s: Omni-Woodpecker is a training-free framework that reduces cross-modal hallucinations in omni LLMs by identifying modality conflicts and rebalancing hidden representations to suppress misleading priors.

2610.30006.t: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders
2610.30006.s: A pipeline using sparse autoencoders extracts interpretable linguistic features from neural detectors, yielding more accurate and explainable AI-generated text classification.

2610.21109.t: Kolab: Benchmarking Human-Agent Collaboration in Long-Horizon Workflows
2610.21109.s: Kolab is a dataset of professional screen recordings that reveals frontier AI agents overestimate collaboration quality and fail to predict expert adoption of contributions in long-horizon workflows.

2610.31819.t: Speculative Diffusion is a Tale of Two Tradeoffs
2610.31819.s: This paper explores trading inference speed for output quality in speculative decoding by jointly adjusting diffusion effort and acceptance leniency to extend the speed-quality Pareto frontier.

2610.23234.t: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
2610.23234.s: MultiAgent-OPD jointly trains a hierarchical multi-agent team via on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning, using a frozen teacher for local process supervision to improve end-to-end performance across multiple datasets.

2610.17821.t: FLOMSS: Generative Music Source Separation by Flow Matching
2610.17821.s: Flow matching is investigated for four-source full-band stereo music separation, evaluating prediction targets, flow paths, modeling strategies, and consistency constraints with both signal-level and perceptual metrics.

2610.01352.t: MMVistaReason: Toward Open-Data and Post-Training Recipes for Multimodal Reasoning
2610.01352.s: MMVistaReason improves open multimodal reasoning through structured data construction, difficulty-aware distillation, and specialized reinforcement learning integration.

2610.24481.t: DuoLM: Fast and Effective Personalized Recommendation with Language Models
2610.24481.s: DuoLM accelerates personalized recommendation by combining a compact encoder and ranker with optimized inference, achieving high throughput with minimal quality loss.

2610.20117.t: KANLab: TensorFlow Playground for Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
2610.20117.s: KANLab is an interactive browser tool for teaching Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks by visualizing B-spline activation curves, gradient descent, and pruning in a compact 2D setting.

2610.27364.t: Predictive Closure: A Set-Level Characterization of JEPA's Feature Selection
2610.27364.s: JEPA feature selection depends on predictive relationships between features rather than individual predictability, allowing unpredictable but relationally useful features to be retained and enabling indirect steering of representations.

2610.31569.t: Echo: Coupled Action and Task Status Signal Denoising for Vision Language Action Models
2610.31569.s: Echo integrates stop and failure signals into a vision-language-action model to guide robot execution and recovery without fine-grained progress labels.

2610.32909.t: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training
2610.32909.s: HoloBoxing learns humanoid boxing by combining a frozen whole-body controller with a compact planner that predicts body-point targets, using imitation initialization and reinforcement learning to refine interaction behavior with minimal additional training.

2610.31572.t: On the Token Collapse Phenomenon in Textual Graph Soft Prompting
2610.31572.s: Graph soft prompting in LLMs suffers from token collapse, where learned graph tokens become indistinguishable and function as generic prompts rather than conveying relational structure, prompting evaluation via alignment probes rather than accuracy alone.

2610.30949.t: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems
2610.30949.s: IQuest-Q1 is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts foundation model trained via multi-stage pre-training, mid-training, and post-training to achieve strong agentic coding and general capabilities.

2610.25100.t: Deep Fusion Memory: A Chunk-Level Parametric Memory for Large Language Models
2610.25100.s: Deep Fusion Memory integrates predicted parametric memory into intermediate hidden states via gated cross-attention, reducing retrieval overhead and improving knowledge-intensive tasks without online retrieval.

2610.27851.t: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions
2610.27851.s: LaLa-World is a language-conditioned latent world model that jointly learns from diverse simulation, robot, and video data to enable efficient model-predictive planning and policy initialization.

2610.30320.t: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
2610.30320.s: FRED improves single-step future video representations in world action models through self-distillation and temporal conditioning, boosting robot policy performance on long-horizon and unseen tasks.

2610.23987.t: What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models
2610.23987.s: GAFU leverages native generation-side representations to improve fine-grained visual understanding in unified multimodal models by compressing them into compact tokens for task-conditioned retrieval.

2610.30753.t: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography
2610.30753.s: FilmFlow is an agentic framework that translates natural-language or video instructions into executable camera trajectories for 3D scenes using specialized director, interpreter, scout, and critic agents, evaluated on the CinemaBench dataset.

2610.30926.t: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation
2610.30926.s: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning enables video diffusion transformers to leverage multimodal language model representations for sparse temporal inference and factor-aware cinematic control through staged grounding and optimization.

2610.25835.t: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages
2610.25835.s: Diffusion language models spend more computation on novel, rare, or incorrect outputs, and decoding speed can improve inference efficiency and reliability.

2610.27712.t: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
2610.27712.s: RLSplat enables feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting with linear reductions in latency, memory, and model size by allocating Gaussians regionally and decoding them via local attention.

2610.19705.t: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing
2610.19705.s: RouteWeaver unifies heterogeneous LLM routing modes via coordinated training and progressive exploration, improving accuracy across diverse reasoning tasks.

2610.28416.t: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V
2610.28416.s: Code2Video-Compass is a benchmark evaluating multimodal language models on code-based video generation across text, image, and video inputs, revealing significant challenges in complex dynamic and state-dependent tasks.

2610.31198.t: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
2610.31198.s: T2Quant improves diffusion language model quantization by dynamically allocating activation precision across denoising steps based on predicted task- and time-dependent sensitivity.

2610.31305.t: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation
2610.31305.s: Cola2 improves hierarchical language generation by jointly optimizing continuous semantic compression, reconstruction-generation balance, and encoder-decoder co-adaptation via dynamic span segmentation, masked diffusion decoding, and flow-matching priors.

2610.31494.t: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding
2610.31494.s: AgentVQA is an offline benchmark assessing vision-language models on realistic agentic tasks across web, robotics, video, games, and spatial planning, revealing that visual grounding and state tracking errors are the primary failure modes.

2610.31062.t: SCOPE: Compiling Natural-Language Policies into Neurosymbolic Predicate Programs
2610.31062.s: SCOPE compiles compound policies into optimized neural-symbolic programs that achieve high accuracy, stability, and interpretability on inexpensive models.

2610.30882.t: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models
2610.30882.s: Reinforcement learning improves reasoning accuracy without requiring a specific wait marker, which originates from training data rather than RL, and automated evaluation metrics can misrepresent reasoning trends.

2610.31623.t: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
2610.31623.s: F2G-Pose is a real-time feed-forward framework that predicts category-level object pose, metric size, and completed shape from a single RGB-D image using dense visual features, DGCNN tokenization, and a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer.

2610.22951.t: MambaAct: Efficient Mamba Action Experts for Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.22951.o: Mohamed Bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
2610.22951.s: MambaAct replaces the transformer action expert in flow-matching VLA policies with a compact Mamba-based expert and a context compressor to cut inference latency while improving robotic manipulation success.

2610.31576.t: What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models
2610.31576.s: Optimized unmasking policies for masked diffusion language models improve efficiency by using trajectory-contraction targets with confidence and hidden states, achieving better speed-accuracy trade-offs with minimal overhead.

2610.28577.s: AKV introduces cache engineering to manage LLM agent key-value caches without altering trajectories, improving efficiency and accuracy via drop and repos operations with a co-designed serving engine.

2610.26659.t: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
2610.26659.s: SpatialScout evaluates vision-language agents on active 3D object mapping, revealing major gaps in precise metric map construction.

2610.28698.t: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
2610.28698.s: Continued pre-training across data scale, diversity, and model size improves embodied learning in virtual worlds but reveals limits in distant-world generalization, motivating richer training beyond imitation.

2610.26828.t: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
2610.26828.s: WildAWM synthesizes controllable computer-use environments and tasks to train general agents via interaction, improving out-of-distribution performance across web, CLI, and GUI benchmarks.

2610.29989.t: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
2610.29989.s: Future Chunk Prediction improves autoregressive video diffusion by enforcing future-chunk supervision, yielding more physically plausible video generation with reduced training cost.

2610.29722.s: LASAGNA evaluates composed RAG pipelines across scales and finds that isolated technique gains do not reliably predict combined retrieval quality, faithfulness, or large-corpus performance.

2610.29680.t: TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking
2610.29680.s: The study proposes a two-stage supervised and adversarial method to synthesize reasoning traces matching a student model's style from teacher answers, improving coding benchmarks without relying on hidden outputs.

2610.29357.t: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
2610.29357.s: Memory-Centric Continual Learning reframes agent memory as an active driver of behavioral improvement through a taxonomy of storage substrates, assets, and policies, a two-loop lifecycle, and scaling frameworks evaluated by retention, adaptation, and transfer.

2610.30120.t: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
2610.30120.s: ALPS is a pretrained visual encoder that unifies physical-state prediction, language alignment, and pixel reconstruction to serve as a shared foundation for world models.

2610.19376.t: DeLoop: Repeated Actions as Self-Supervision for Long-Horizon Agents
2610.19376.s: DeLoop is a self-supervised preference optimization method that reduces repetitive tool-use loops in language-model agents by learning from their own rollouts, improving efficiency and success under context compression.

2610.29545.t: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
2610.29545.s: PACE is a post-hoc four-bit quantizer for linear-attention recurrent states that rounds less frequently and uses column-wise scales to reduce error, enabling lower memory usage without fine-tuning.

2610.29441.t: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
2610.29441.s: ALLOT is a training-free method that allocates block-sparse attention densities across layer-step pairs in video diffusion transformers to maximize output fidelity under a latency budget.

2610.30023.t: RealMe: Immersive Volumetric Video from Minimal Captures
2610.30023.s: RealMe enhances sparse, low-resolution multi-view captures into high-resolution, 4D-consistent videos using a video diffusion model with layout-aware attention and frequency-domain latent supervision for volumetric reconstruction.

2610.23344.t: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
2610.23344.s: LM2LM uses a frozen research world model to provide scalable reinforcement learning rewards for generating language model improvements, maintaining reliability through periodic real execution and outperforming larger baselines at lower cost.

2610.11942.t: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents
2610.11942.s: A decoder-free, action-conditioned world model predicts next-screen representations to verify GUI transitions and detect hijacked screens with high accuracy and low latency.

2610.21204.t: Entertain, then Cancel: How Thinking Makes Reasoning Models Read Some and Or Literally
2610.21204.s: Extended reasoning in language models suppresses everyday scalar implicatures by initially considering enriched interpretations before canceling them, though early-stage answers can recover these inferences.

2610.30066.s: Looping early Transformer layers improves training and inference efficiency of uniform diffusion language models without altering their objective or sampler.

2610.29934.t: ToM2Vec: Continuous Theory-of-Mind Tokens for Multi-Agent Coordination
2610.29934.o: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
2610.29934.s: ToM2Vec learns abstract partner-state representations via continuous latent reasoning tokens to improve multi-agent collaboration across diverse settings.

2610.27040.t: ACE-Brain-0.6: Scaling Spatial Grounding for Physical Foundation Models
2610.27040.s: Scaling diverse verifiable visual grounding data improves spatial perception and embodied manipulation performance in open multimodal models.

2610.26836.t: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy
2610.26836.s: Agent harnesses that retrieve long simulator outputs from files rather than including them in context cause GPT models to substitute their own approximations for authoritative results, reducing accuracy despite correct underlying computations.

2610.22659.t: Exploring The Empirical Privacy Landscape of Synthetic Data
2610.22659.s: Privacy-aware rewriting of synthetic medical records improves privacy protection with less capability loss than direct fine-tuning or DP-SGD, offering a favorable trade-off for sensitive data.

2610.30090.t: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift
2610.30090.s: VX-One is a small multi-task neural network that outputs calibrated typed decision primitives for perimeter triage, evaluated in a two-phase cascade against signature engines and baseline classifiers across multiple intrusion detection benchmarks.

2610.27861.t: RoboCasa-Shift: Stage-Aware Robustness Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Policies in Long-Horizon Household Manipulation
2610.27861.s: RoboCasa-Shift evaluates vision-language-action robustness through paired rollouts and stage-aware diagnostics, revealing that failure patterns vary by shift factor and task rather than degrading uniformly.

2610.27999.t: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
2610.27999.s: Matrix-Game 4.0 separates game logic from visual synthesis via an executable engine and autoregressive video renderer, achieving real-time interactive gameplay with low latency.

2610.28578.t: Sage-A1.5: From Long-Horizon Execution to Scientific Exploration with Capability Composition
2610.28578.s: Sage-A1.5 is a 35B mixture-of-experts agentic model that improves long-horizon problem solving via adaptive task delegation, verification, and open scientific exploration.

2610.28630.s: SolarRenderer adapts a frozen video backbone with lightweight LoRAs to render realistic videos from diverse structural inputs in four steps or real-time streaming, using frame-aligned training data.

2610.28594.t: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
2610.28594.s: Video-Point Model predicts future multi-view videos and 3D point trajectories from video histories and instructions, improving forecasting and robot control through shared 3D-aware representations.

2610.25078.t: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
2610.25078.s: CoEvo-RSI reduces brain-body mismatch in recursive self-improving agents by using bidirectional historical inheritance to align model capabilities with evolving harness requirements, achieving strong results via supervised fine-tuning.

2610.14136.s: A correction module trained to refine diffusion predictions reduces exposure bias, improving unguided sample quality and enabling distillation to eliminate inference overhead.

2610.27628.t: PAR: Progress-Aligned Recurrence for Length Generalization in State Tracking
2610.27628.s: Progress-Aligned Recurrence trains looped language models to match intermediate states and stabilize recurrent norms, enabling strong length extrapolation on sequential tracking tasks.

2610.28354.t: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
2610.28354.s: S-Agent 2.0 improves spatial reasoning by integrating a persistent scene memory and plain-language interpretation into a coding agent with 3D perception tools.

2610.25844.t: SWIFT: Self-guided Weak-to-strong dIFfusion models via Target extrapolation
2610.25844.s: Swift improves diffusion model training by extrapolating regression targets away from a frozen weak denoiser, reducing error and training cost without inference overhead.

2610.18604.t: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
2610.18604.s: LLM2R treats 3D part assembly as sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only LLM, using geometric tokens and learnable summary tokens to predict all part poses in a single pass with improved scalability and accuracy.

2610.28522.t: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems
2610.28522.s: DecisionPivot is a diagnostic benchmark that evaluates decision models across controlled variations, revealing gaps between aggregate accuracy, contrast-group performance, calibration, and reasoning effort.

2610.28601.s: Agent S4 autonomously evolves computer-use interfaces from task experience, significantly improving open-source agent performance and reducing costs compared to larger proprietary models.

2511.14102.t: Specter: Fast MoE Inference via Quantization-Enabled Multi-Step Speculative Offloading
2511.14102.s: Specter accelerates single-GPU mixture-of-experts inference by combining quantized speculative decoding with expert offloading to hide PCIe latency and improve throughput.

2610.28559.s: A large-scale continuous flow language model achieves efficient training, high-quality generation, and faster inference through blockwise flow design, self-speculative decoding, and multi-token prediction.

2610.16523.t: EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents
2610.16523.s: EAU is a meta-agent framework that co-evolves the user simulator, environment, and reinforcement learning setup alongside the policy to improve multi-turn LLM agent training.

2610.24628.t: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model
2610.24628.s: Muse Glimmer is a 30B-parameter open-source causal language model with a perception encoder that performs multi-step reasoning and tool use locally on consumer hardware via 4-bit quantization.

2610.27435.t: Harness Self-Evolution for Long-Horizon Terminal Agents
2610.27435.s: RiseHarness iteratively improves agent harness reliability by analyzing execution traces and integrating mechanisms from other frameworks without altering model weights.

2610.25043.t: VLA-Rolling: Fewer Denoising Steps, Better Control via Adaptive Action Reuse
2610.25043.s: VLA-Rolling improves vision-language-action model efficiency by reusing discarded action tails with adaptive denoising budgets, reducing inference cost and boosting success rates.

2610.24899.t: HybridResearcher: Bridging the Structured-Unstructured Boundary for Deep Research Agents
2610.24899.s: HybridResearcher is a small agent trained via synthetic cross-source trajectories and reinforcement learning to reason across structured and unstructured data, outperforming much larger models without forgetting single-source skills.

2610.24649.t: Good Judgment, Bad Advice: Decision-Model Controllers Raise Agent Cost Without Improving Success
2610.24649.s: A typed decision model consulted at fixed points increased agent costs without improving success rates, despite better ranking of finish requests, due to poor calibration.

2610.27406.t: More Memory, Worse Agents: Error Reproduction and Anti-Persistence in LLM Agents
2610.27406.s: Anti-Persistence improves LLM agent self-improvement by accumulating execution experience while discarding synthesized guidance after use, reducing error reproduction and cost.

2610.28074.t: Slot-JEPA: Object-Structured Prediction Interfaces for Latent World Models
2610.28074.s: Slot-JEPA decomposes dense representations into reusable semantic slots and spatial masks to improve predictive modeling, planning, and transfer across visual tasks.

2610.28435.t: Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision
2610.28435.s: A general vision-language model can serve as a multimodal reranker via single-pass choice questions, matching or exceeding dedicated rerankers with minimal tuning.

2606.31002.t: Beyond Compilation: Evaluating Faithful Natural-Language-to-Lean Statement Formalization
2606.31002.s: The study evaluates whether Lean compilation alone ensures faithful statement autoformalization, finding substantial gaps between compiling and semantically accepted outputs across multiple systems, with tool-augmented agents improving compilation but still exhibiting real translation errors.

2610.27914.s: ConfigWM uses task descriptions to steer visual embeddings into task-specific state spaces, filtering irrelevant noise for robust planning.
